title.zh: 卷四百八十三 列傳第二百四十二 世家六 湖南周氏周行逢(子:保權 附:李觀象 張文表) 荆南高氏高保融(弟:保勗 子:繼沖 弟:保寅 附:孫光憲 梁延嗣 漳泉留氏留從效 陳氏陳洪進(子:文顯 文顥 文顗 文頊)
title.en: Volume 483 Biographies 242: Hereditary Houses 6 - Hu and southern Zhou clans Zhou Xingfeng (son: Bao Quan, relative: Li Guanxiang, Zhang Wenbiao), Jing and southern Gao clans Gao Baorong (younger brother: Bao Xu, sons: Ji Chong, younger brother: Bao Yin, relative: Sun Guangxian, Liang Yansi, Zhang Quanliu remaining clan member nephew, Chen clan Chen Hongjin (sons: Wen Xian, Wen Hao, Wen Yi, Wen Xu)

sentences.zh: 世家六○湖南周氏荊南高氏漳泉留氏陳氏

translations.literal: Hereditary Houses 6: The Zhou clan of Hunan, the Gao clan of Jingnan, the Liu clan of Zhang and Quan, and the Chen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary Houses 6 — the Zhou of Hunan, the Gao of Jingnan, the Liu of Zhang and Quan, and the Chen.

sentences.zh: 湖南周氏周行逢

translations.literal: The Zhou clan of Hunan: Zhou Xingfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou of Hunan — Zhou Xingfeng

sentences.zh: 湖南周行逢，朗州武陵人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xingfeng of Hunan was a native of Wuling in Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng of Hunan came from Wuling in Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少無賴，不事產業。

translations.literal: In youth he was a ruffian and did not attend to any trade or property.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was a wastrel who paid no heed to honest livelihood.

sentences.zh: 嘗犯法配隸鎮兵，以驍勇累遷裨校。

translations.literal: He once broke the law and was assigned to serve as a garrison soldier; through valor in battle he was repeatedly promoted to adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: After a conviction he was conscripted into the frontier garrison, and his fighting prowess won him repeated promotions to adjutant rank.

sentences.zh: 自唐乾寧二年，馬氏專有湖南二十州之地，雖稟朝廷正朔，其郡守官屬皆自署。

translations.literal: From the second year of Qianning in Tang, the Ma clan alone held the twenty prefectures of Hunan; although they acknowledged the court calendar, their prefects and officials were all appointed by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang Qianning year 2 onward the Ma clan controlled all twenty Hunan prefectures; they observed the imperial calendar in name, but every prefect and official was their own appointment.

sentences.zh: 至周廣順初，兄弟爭國，求援於江南李景，景遣大將邊鎬率兵赴之，因下長沙，遷馬氏之族於建康，封希萼為楚王，居洪州，希崇鎮舒，居揚州。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Guangshun under Zhou, the brothers fought over the realm and sought aid from Li Jing of Jiangnan; Jing sent the great general Bian Hao with troops to their aid, who thereby took Changsha, moved the Ma clan to Jiankang, enfeoffed Xi'e as King of Chu and settled him at Hongzhou, and had Xi'chong guard Shu and reside at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou Guangshun the Ma brothers fell into civil war and called on Li Jing of Jiangnan, who sent his general Bian Hao south. Bian seized Changsha, relocated the Ma family to Jiankang, made Xi'e King of Chu at Hongzhou, and posted Xi'chong to Yangzhou after assigning him Shu.

sentences.zh: 宋興，希崇率兄弟十七人歸朝，皆為美官。

translations.literal: When Song arose, Xi'chong led seventeen brothers to submit to the court, and all received fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Song, Xi'chong brought seventeen brothers to court and each was rewarded with a handsome post.

sentences.zh: 景以鎬為潭帥。

translations.literal: Jing made Hao commander of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing installed Bian Hao as military governor of Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會朗州眾亂，推衙將劉言為留後，言以行逢為都指揮使。

translations.literal: At that time Lang Prefecture rose in disorder; the troops pushed the yamen officer Liu Yan as acting governor, and Yan made Xingfeng overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Lang Prefecture mutinied and elevated the yamen officer Liu Yan as acting governor; Yan appointed Xingfeng commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 行逢以眾情表於景，請授言節鉞，景不從。

translations.literal: Xingfeng presented the troops' wishes to Jing and requested that Yan be granted the command seal; Jing did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng petitioned Li Jing on behalf of the army to invest Liu Yan with full authority, but Jing refused.

sentences.zh: 召言入金陵，言懼，遣副使王進逵、行軍何景真與行逢帥舟師襲破潭州，鎬遁去，行逢等據其城。

translations.literal: Jing summoned Yan to Jinling; Yan grew afraid and sent his deputy Wang Jinkui, the campaign officer He Jingzhen, and Xingfeng to lead a fleet that stormed and took Tanzhou; Hao fled, and Xingfeng and the others held the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing summoned Yan to Jinling, Yan panicked and sent his deputy Wang Jinkui, campaign officer He Jingzhen, and Xingfeng with a river fleet against Tanzhou. Bian Hao fled, and Xingfeng's force occupied the city.

sentences.zh: 言遣使上言長沙兵亂，焚燒公府，請移治朗州。

translations.literal: Yan sent envoys to report upward that Changsha had military disorder and that the government offices were burned, requesting that the seat of government be moved to Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan reported to the throne that troops had ravaged Changsha and burned the government compound, and asked to move his headquarters to Lang.

sentences.zh: 周祖即以言為朗帥，王進逵為潭帥，行逢為潭州行軍司馬、領集州刺史。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder thereupon made Yan commander of Lang, Wang Jinkui commander of Tan, and Xingfeng campaign marshal of Tanzhou while also holding the post of prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder confirmed Yan as governor of Lang, Wang Jinkui as governor of Tan, and Xingfeng as Tan's campaign marshal with concurrent appointment as prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進逵寇朗州，害劉言，周祖即以進逵為朗州節度，以行逢領鄂州節度、知潭州軍府事。

translations.literal: Before long Jinkui raided Lang Prefecture and killed Liu Yan; the Zhou founder then made Jinkui military governor of Lang and had Xingfeng hold the Ezhou command while administering Tanzhou's military government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Jinkui attacked Lang, killed Liu Yan, and was made Lang's military governor; Xingfeng received the Ezhou command and took charge of Tan's military administration.

sentences.zh: 初，朗州人謂劉言為「劉咬牙」，馬氏將亂，湘中童謠云：「馬去不用鞭咬牙過今年。」

translations.literal: Earlier the people of Lang had called Liu Yan "Liu Gnashing Teeth." When the Ma clan was about to fall into disorder, a children's rhyme in Xiang ran: "When the Ma go, no whip is needed; Gnashing Teeth passes this year."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Lang had nicknamed Liu Yan "Liu Gnashing Teeth." As the Ma regime crumbled, a Hunan children's rhyme said, "When the Ma depart you need no whip — Gnashing Teeth will pass this year."

sentences.zh: 及邊鎬俘馬氏，鎬為劉言所逐，而言亦被害。

translations.literal: When Bian Hao captured the Ma clan, Hao was driven off by Liu Yan, and Yan too was later killed.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao had taken the Ma captive, only to be expelled by Liu Yan — and Yan himself was slain in turn.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，世宗將用師淮甸，詔朗州王進逵出師入鄂州界，進逵遣裨將潘叔嗣領兵五千為先鋒。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era, Shizong was about to use troops in the Huai region and ordered Wang Jinkui of Lang to march into the borders of Ezhou; Jinkui sent the adjutant Pan Shusi with five thousand men as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiande, Emperor Shizong prepared a campaign on the Huai and ordered Wang Jinkui of Lang into Ezhou territory; Jinkui sent adjutant Pan Shusi ahead with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 行及鄂州界，叔嗣乃回戈襲進逵，進逵聞之，倍道先入武陵。

translations.literal: When they reached the border of Ezhou, Shusi turned his weapons and struck Jinkui; on hearing this Jinkui doubled his pace and entered Wuling first.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ezhou frontier Shusi wheeled about and attacked Jinkui, who forced a rapid march to reach Wuling ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 叔嗣攻其城，進逵敗走，為叔嗣所殺，迎行逢為節度。

translations.literal: Shusi assaulted the city; Jinkui was defeated and fled and was killed by Shusi, who then welcomed Xingfeng as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Shusi stormed the city, routed Jinkui, and killed him, then installed Xingfeng as military governor.

sentences.zh: 行逢至，即斬叔嗣以徇。

translations.literal: When Xingfeng arrived, he immediately beheaded Shusi as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng arrived and at once executed Shusi before the troops as an example.

sentences.zh: 世宗乃授行逢郎州大都督、武平軍節度、製置武安靜江等州軍事兼侍中，盡有湖南之地。

translations.literal: Shizong then invested Xingfeng as great governor of Lang, military governor of the Wuping army, commissioner for the military affairs of Wu'an, Jingjiang, and other prefectures, and concurrently Palace Attendant, so that he held all the lands of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong appointed Xingfeng great governor of Lang, military governor of Wuping, commissioner over Wu'an, Jingjiang, and related prefectures, and Palace Attendant — giving him the whole of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加兼中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was further given the concurrent post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was also made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 行逢在鎮，盡心為治，辟署官屬，必取廉介之士。

translations.literal: While Xingfeng held the commandery he devoted himself wholeheartedly to governance; in appointing officials he always chose men of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In his domain Xingfeng governed conscientiously and staffed his administration only with upright, incorruptible men.

sentences.zh: 有女婿求補吏，不許，返給以耒耜，語之曰：「吏所以治民也，汝才不能任職，豈敢私汝以祿邪？

translations.literal: A son-in-law sought appointment as an official; he refused and instead gave him farming tools, saying: "Officials exist to govern the people. Your talent cannot bear office — how dare I privately grant you a salary?
translations.idiomatic: When a son-in-law asked for an official post he refused and sent him home with plow and hoe, saying, "Office exists to serve the people. You lack the ability — how could I give you a salary out of favoritism?

sentences.zh: 姑歸墾田以自活。」

translations.literal: For now return and till the fields to support yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Go back and farm for your living for the time being."

sentences.zh: 其公正多此類。

translations.literal: His fairness had many examples of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such acts of impartiality were typical of him.

sentences.zh: 條教簡約，民皆悅之。

translations.literal: His regulations were simple and concise, and the people all rejoiced in them.
translations.idiomatic: His laws were plain and spare, and the people welcomed them.

sentences.zh: 然性多猜忌，左右少有忤意者必置於法，麾下之人重足累息。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was much given to suspicion; anyone close to him who slightly displeased him was sure to be punished by law, and those under his command walked on tiptoe and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was deeply suspicious: the slightest offense among his intimates brought legal punishment, and his subordinates lived in constant fear.

sentences.zh: 有何景山者，為王進逵記室，常狎侮行逢。

translations.literal: There was one He Jingshan, who had been recorder for Wang Jinkui and often treated Xingfeng with coarse familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: He Jingshan had served as Wang Jinkui's recorder and habitually treated Xingfeng with disrespect.

sentences.zh: 及行逢為帥，署景山益陽令，數月，縛投於江。

translations.literal: When Xingfeng became commander he appointed Jingshan magistrate of Yiyang; after several months he had him bound and cast into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xingfeng became governor he made Jingshan magistrate of Yiyang, but within months had him bound and thrown into the river.

sentences.zh: 又館驛巡官鄧洵美與翰林學士李昉同年進士，會昉使行逢，召至傳舍，與話終日。

translations.literal: Also the postal-station inspector Deng Xunmei and the Hanlin academician Li Fang had passed the jinshi examination in the same year; when Fang was sent on mission to Xingfeng, Xunmei was summoned to the relay lodge and talked with him the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Postal inspector Deng Xunmei and Hanlin academician Li Fang had been jinshi classmates; when Fang visited Xingfeng on mission, Xunmei was called to the guesthouse and they talked all day.

sentences.zh: 行逢疑其泄己陰事，黜為易俗場官，潛遣殺之。

translations.literal: Xingfeng suspected that he had divulged his private affairs, demoted him to an officer at Yisu post, and secretly sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng suspected he had betrayed confidential matters, demoted him to a minor post at Yisu, and had him assassinated in secret.

sentences.zh: 由是士流不附。

translations.literal: Because of this the scholar-official class would not attach itself to him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the educated elite kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 馬氏舊僚有天策府學士徐仲雅，性滑稽，頗恃才倨傲，行逢以為節度判官。

translations.literal: Among the former retainers of the Ma clan was the Tiancesi academician Xu Zhongya, witty in nature and rather arrogant in reliance on his talent; Xingfeng made him military governor's aide.
translations.idiomatic: A former Ma retainer, Tiancesi academician Xu Zhongya, was witty and rather arrogant about his gifts; Xingfeng appointed him military governor's aide.

sentences.zh: 行逢多署溪洞蠻酋為司空、太保，一日謂仲雅曰：「吾奄有湖湘，兵強俗阜，四鄰其懼我乎？」

translations.literal: Xingfeng often appointed chieftains of the stream-cave Miao as Grandees and Grand Guardians; one day he said to Zhongya: "I now hold all of Huguang and Hunan, with strong troops and a prosperous people — do the neighbors fear me?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng frequently gave tribal chiefs of the hill country honorary titles as Grandee or Grand Guardian. One day he asked Zhongya, "I hold all the lakes and Xiang region, with strong armies and a thriving populace — do our neighbors fear us?"

sentences.zh: 仲雅曰：「公部內司空滿川，太保遍地，孰敢不懼？」

translations.literal: Zhongya said: "Within your command Grandees fill every stream and Grand Guardians cover every field — who would not fear?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongya replied, "Within your borders Grandees choke every river and Grand Guardians blanket every field — who would not be afraid?"

sentences.zh: 行逢不悅，擯斥仲雅。

translations.literal: Xingfeng was displeased and drove Zhongya away.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng took offense and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 行逢妻潘氏貌醜，性剛狠。

translations.literal: Xingfeng's wife, the Pan clan, was ugly in appearance and fierce and harsh in nature.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng's wife Lady Pan was plain of face and stern and unyielding in temperament.

sentences.zh: 行逢為帥，妻不為屈，不入府署，躬率奴仆耕織以自給，賦調必先期輸送。

translations.literal: When Xingfeng became commander his wife would not yield to him, would not enter the government offices, personally led slaves and servants in farming and weaving to support herself, and always delivered tax levies ahead of the due date.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he became governor she refused to defer to him or enter his headquarters, led her servants in farming and weaving to support the household, and always paid taxes before they were due.

sentences.zh: 行逢止之，不從，曰：「稅，官物也，若主帥自免其家，何以率下？」

translations.literal: Xingfeng tried to stop her but she would not obey, saying: "Taxes are state property — if the commander exempts his own household, how can he lead those below?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng urged her to stop, but she refused, saying, "Taxes belong to the state. If the commander exempts his own family, how can he command others?"

sentences.zh: 建隆三年十月，行逢卒，追封汝南郡王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Jianlong, Xingfeng died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Runan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jianlong 3 Xingfeng died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 子 保權

translations.literal: Son: Baoquan.
translations.idiomatic: Son — Baoquan

sentences.zh: 子保權，年十一。

translations.literal: His son Baoquan was eleven years old.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoquan was eleven.

sentences.zh: 初為武平軍節度副使，太祖授以起復檢校太尉、朗州大都督、武平軍節度。

translations.literal: He had first been deputy military governor of the Wuping army; the Taizu invested him, returning from mourning, as acting Grand Commandant, great governor of Lang, and military governor of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as deputy military governor of Wuping; Taizu recalled him from mourning to appoint him acting Grand Commandant, great governor of Lang, and military governor of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 初，行逢疾且亟，召將校托保權曰：「吾部內凶狠者誅之略盡，唯張文表在焉，吾死，文表必亂。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xingfeng's illness was grave and urgent, he summoned his generals and entrusted Baoquan, saying: "I have executed nearly all the fierce men within my command; only Zhang Wenbiao remains. When I die Wenbiao is sure to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: As Xingfeng lay dying he gathered his officers and entrusted Baoquan to them, saying, "I have killed nearly every dangerous man in my ranks except Zhang Wenbiao. When I am gone he will surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 諸公善佐吾兒，無失土宇，必不得已，當舉族歸朝，無令陷於虎口。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen must well assist my son, do not lose our territory; if there is truly no alternative, then lead the whole clan to submit to the court — do not let them fall into a tiger's maw."
translations.idiomatic: Support my son faithfully and hold our lands. If you truly cannot, bring the whole clan to court — do not let them fall into the tiger's jaws."

sentences.zh: 行逢卒，明年春，文表果自衡州舉兵據潭州，將取朗陵，盡滅周氏。

translations.literal: When Xingfeng died, the next spring Wenbiao indeed raised troops from Hengzhou, seized Tanzhou, and was about to take Langling and exterminate the Zhou clan entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingfeng's death, the following spring Wenbiao rose from Hengzhou, seized Tanzhou, and marched on Langling intent on wiping out the Zhou house.

sentences.zh: 保權乞師於朝廷，江陵高繼衝亦以其事聞。

translations.literal: Baoquan begged troops from the court, and Gao Jichong of Jiangling also reported the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Baoquan appealed to the court for troops, and Gao Jichong at Jiangling reported the crisis as well.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使趙遂齎詔諭文表，而保權之奏繼至。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the palace envoy Zhao Sui bearing an edict to instruct Wenbiao, while Baoquan's memorials continued to arrive in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched palace envoy Zhao Sui with an edict to admonish Wenbiao, even as Baoquan's urgent reports kept arriving.

sentences.zh: 乃遣山南東道節度慕容延釗為湖南道行營都部署，宣徽南院使李處耘為都監，率淄州刺史尹崇珂、申州刺史聶章、郢州刺史趙重進、判四方館事武懷節、氈毯使張繼勳、染院副使康延澤、內酒坊副使盧懷忠等將步騎往平之，又發安、復等十州兵會於襄陽。

translations.literal: He then sent the Shannan East Circuit military governor Murong Yanjiao as overall commander of the Hunan campaign headquarters, the Southern Bureau commissioner of the Privy Secretariat Li Chuyun as overall supervisor, leading the Zizhou prefect Yin Chongke, Shenzhou prefect Nie Zhang, Yingzhou prefect Zhao Chongjin, Four Directions Hostel judge Wu Huaijie, felt-rug envoy Zhang Jixun, dye-house vice commissioner Kang Yanze, inner wine-workshop vice commissioner Lu Huaizhong, and others with infantry and cavalry to pacify the rebellion, and also mobilized troops from An, Fu, and nine other prefectures to assemble at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Shannan East military governor Murong Yanjiao overall commander of the Hunan campaign, with Privy Secretariat commissioner Li Chuyun as supervisor, and sent Yin Chongke of Zi, Nie Zhang of Shen, Zhao Chongjin of Ying, Wu Huaijie, Zhang Jixun, Kang Yanze, Lu Huaizhong, and others with infantry and cavalry to suppress the revolt, while ten prefectures including An and Fu converged their forces at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 師及江陵，趙遂至潭州，文表已為保權之眾所殺。

translations.literal: When the army reached Jiangling, Zhao Sui arrived at Tanzhou — Wenbiao had already been killed by Baoquan's troops.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the army reached Jiangling and Zhao Sui reached Tanzhou, Baoquan's forces had already killed Wenbiao.

sentences.zh: 保權牙校張從富輩，以為文表已平而王師繼進不已，懼為襲取，相與拒守。

translations.literal: Baoquan's military officers Zhang Congfu and his fellows, believing that Wenbiao was already pacified yet the imperial army continued to advance without cease, feared they would be seized and together held out in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Baoquan's officers Zhang Congfu and others, believing Wenbiao was crushed yet the imperial army still advancing, feared annexation and banded together to resist.

sentences.zh: 延釗令閣門使丁德裕先路安撫。

translations.literal: Yanjiao ordered the Gatekeeper Commissioner Ding Deyu to go ahead on the route to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjiao sent Gatekeeper Commissioner Ding Deyu ahead to offer reassurance.

sentences.zh: 及至城下，從富輩拒而不納，盡撤部內橋梁，沉舫伐樹塞路。

translations.literal: When he reached the city walls, Congfu and his fellows refused entry, removed all bridges within the command, sank boats, felled trees, and blocked the roads.
translations.idiomatic: At the walls Congfu's party refused him entry, tore down every bridge in the district, sank boats, and felled trees to block the roads.

sentences.zh: 德裕以不奉詔不敢與戰，退軍以須朝旨。

translations.literal: Deyu, because he had not received orders to fight, dared not engage and withdrew his troops to await court instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking orders to fight, Deyu dared not engage and withdrew to await imperial command.

sentences.zh: 延釗以聞，太祖遣中使諭保權及將校曰：「爾本請師救援，故發大軍以拯爾難。

translations.literal: Yanjiao reported this; Taizu sent a palace envoy to instruct Baoquan and the officers: "You yourselves begged for troops to rescue you, and so a great army was sent to save you from disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjiao reported upward, and Taizu sent a palace envoy to tell Baoquan and his officers, "You yourselves asked for rescue, and we sent a great army to deliver you.

sentences.zh: 今妖孽既殄，是有大造於爾輩，反拒王師何也？

translations.literal: Now that the evil has been exterminated, we have shown you great favor — why do you turn and resist the imperial army?
translations.idiomatic: The rebel is destroyed and we have done you a great kindness — why do you now bar the imperial army?

sentences.zh: 無自取塗炭，重擾生聚。」

translations.literal: Do not bring ruin on yourselves and again disturb the living populace."
translations.idiomatic: Do not invite destruction upon yourselves and bring fresh misery to the people."

sentences.zh: 何權出軍於澧州南，未及交鋒，望風而潰。

translations.literal: He Quan led troops out south of Lizhou; before battle was joined they broke and fled at sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He Quan marched out south of Li Prefecture, but his force scattered at the first sight of the imperial army without even fighting.

sentences.zh: 復還朗州，焚廬舍廩庫皆盡，驅略居人奔竄山谷，城郭為之一空。

translations.literal: They returned again to Lang Prefecture, burned dwellings and granaries to the last, drove and plundered the inhabitants who fled into mountain valleys, and the city and suburbs were left utterly empty.
translations.idiomatic: They fell back on Lang, burned every dwelling and granary, drove the populace into the hills, and left the city a wasteland.

sentences.zh: 王師長驅而南，獲從富於西山下，梟首朗市。

translations.literal: The imperial army pressed south in long marches, captured Congfu at the western hills, and displayed his head in the market of Lang.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army drove south, took Congfu at the western hills, and exposed his head in Lang's market.

sentences.zh: 其大將汪端劫保權並家屬，棄城亡匿山洞，王師至數月，獲保權。

translations.literal: His great general Wang Duan seized Baoquan together with his family, abandoned the city and hid in mountain caves; when the imperial army arrived months later they recovered Baoquan.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Duan seized Baoquan and his family, abandoned the city, and hid in the mountains; months after the imperial army arrived they recovered Baoquan.

sentences.zh: 武懷節分兵克岳州，端擁保權眾寇略，未幾亦就擒，礫於市，湖湘悉平。

translations.literal: Wu Huaijie divided troops and took Yuezhou; Duan with Baoquan's followers raided and plundered, but before long he too was captured and dismembered in the market, and Huguang and Hunan were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Huaijie detached a force that took Yuezhou; Duan led Baoquan's remnant in raids but was soon captured and executed by dismemberment in the market, and all of Huguang and Hunan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 附 李觀象

translations.literal: Appended: Li Guanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography — Li Guanxiang

sentences.zh: 李觀象，桂州臨桂人。

translations.literal: Li Guanxiang was a native of Lingui in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guanxiang came from Lingui in Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 行逢署為掌書記。

translations.literal: Xingfeng appointed him recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng appointed him chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 行逢性殘忍，多誅殺。

translations.literal: Xingfeng's nature was cruel and he executed many.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng was cruel by nature and put many to death.

sentences.zh: 觀象懼及禍，清苦自勵，以求知遇，帳幃、寢衣悉以紙為之。

translations.literal: Guanxiang feared he would meet with disaster, disciplined himself in austerity to seek favor, and made all his curtains and sleeping garments of paper.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, Guanxiang lived in deliberate austerity to win trust — even his curtains and bedding were made of paper.

sentences.zh: 行逢頗加信任，軍府之政一皆取決。

translations.literal: Xingfeng greatly increased his trust, and all military-government affairs were decided solely by him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng came to rely on him heavily, and every matter of the military government passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 觀象涉經史，有文辭，忌才怙寵，湖南士人多為所排擯。

translations.literal: Guanxiang was versed in the classics and histories and had literary talent, but he envied ability and relied on favor; many Hunan scholars were driven away by him.
translations.idiomatic: Guanxiang was learned in the classics and histories and wrote well, but he envied talent and abused his influence, driving out many Hunan scholars.

sentences.zh: 行逢臨終托以後事，令其子保權善待之。

translations.literal: At his deathbed Xingfeng entrusted him with later affairs and ordered his son Baoquan to treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Xingfeng entrusted affairs to him and told his son Baoquan to treat him kindly.

sentences.zh: 及張文表難作，王師壓境，觀象謂保權曰：「我所恃者北有荊渚，以為唇齒，今高氏拱手聽命，朗州勢不獨全，莫若幅巾歸朝，則不失富貴。」

translations.literal: When Zhang Wenbiao's trouble arose and the imperial army pressed the borders, Guanxiang said to Baoquan: "What I relied on was that to the north we had Jing and Chu as lip and teeth; now the Gao clan bows and obeys orders — Lang Prefecture cannot stand alone. Better to go to court in plain dress, and you will not lose wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbiao rebelled and the imperial army approached, Guanxiang told Baoquan, "I counted on Jingchu to the north as our ally, but the Gao have already submitted. Lang cannot stand alone — better go to court in plain dress and keep your wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 保權幼懦，不能用其言。

translations.literal: Baoquan was young and timid and could not use his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Young and timid, Baoquan would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 及湖湘平，太祖聞觀象嘗為保權畫謀，以為左補闕。

translations.literal: When Huguang and Hunan were pacified, Taizu heard that Guanxiang had once drawn up plans for Baoquan and made him Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: After Huguang and Hunan were pacified, Taizu learned Guanxiang had advised Baoquan and appointed him Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 附 張文表

translations.literal: Appended: Zhang Wenbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography — Zhang Wenbiao

sentences.zh: 張文表，朗州武陵人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenbiao was a native of Wuling in Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenbiao came from Wuling in Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從王進逵、周行逢舉兵逐邊鎬，行逢署文表衡州刺史，頗心忌之，常欲誅文表，未有以發。

translations.literal: He followed Wang Jinkui and Zhou Xingfeng in raising troops to drive off Bian Hao; Xingfeng appointed Wenbiao prefect of Hengzhou but was much jealous of him in heart, often wishing to execute Wenbiao yet never finding cause.
translations.idiomatic: He had followed Wang Jinkui and Zhou Xingfeng in driving out Bian Hao; Xingfeng made him prefect of Heng but deeply mistrusted him and long wished to kill him without finding occasion.

sentences.zh: 及行逢卒，保權遣兵代永州戍卒，路出衡陽，文表遂驅之以襲潭州。

translations.literal: When Xingfeng died, Baoquan sent troops to relieve the Yongzhou garrison; their route passed through Hengyang, and Wenbiao drove them on to strike Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingfeng's death Baoquan sent troops to relieve the Yongzhou garrison; passing through Hengyang, Wenbiao turned them against Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時行軍司馬廖簡知留後，素輕文表，不為之備。

translations.literal: At that time the campaign marshal Liao Jian was acting governor; he had always looked down on Wenbiao and made no preparations against him.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign marshal Liao Jian was acting governor; he had always despised Wenbiao and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 方宴飲，外報文表兵至，簡殊不以介意，謂四坐曰：「此黃口小兒，至則成擒，何足患也？」

translations.literal: He was just at a banquet when word came from outside that Wenbiao's troops had arrived; Jian paid it no mind at all and said to those seated: "This yellow-mouthed boy — when he comes he will be captured at once; what is there to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: He was feasting when word came that Wenbiao's army had arrived. Jian scarcely cared and told the company, "This beardless boy will be taken the moment he shows himself — what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 飲啖如故。

translations.literal: He drank and ate as before.
translations.idiomatic: He continued eating and drinking as before.

sentences.zh: 俄文表率眾徑入府中，簡醉不能彀弓弩，但按膝叱之，文表遂害簡及坐客十餘人。

translations.literal: Before long Wenbiao led his crowd straight into the government offices; Jian, drunk, could not draw the bow, but only pressed his knee and shouted at them — Wenbiao then killed Jian and more than ten guests at the table.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wenbiao burst into the headquarters. Too drunk to string his bow, Jian could only slap his knee and shout — whereupon Wenbiao killed him and more than ten guests.

sentences.zh: 保權遣其將楊師璠悉眾以禦文表，保權泣謂眾曰：「先君可謂知人矣。

translations.literal: Baoquan sent his general Yang Shibao with the full force to resist Wenbiao; Baoquan wept and said to the troops: "My late father may truly be called one who knew men.
translations.idiomatic: Baoquan sent general Yang Shibao with the full army against Wenbiao and wept before the troops, saying, "My father truly knew men.

sentences.zh: 今墳土未幹，文表構逆，軍府安危，在此一舉，諸公勉之！」

translations.literal: Now the grave earth is not yet dry and Wenbiao has raised rebellion; the safety of the military government hangs on this one effort — gentlemen, exert yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: His grave is still fresh and Wenbiao rebels — the fate of our command rests on this battle. Do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆感憤，遂破其眾於平津亭，擒文表臠而食之。

translations.literal: The troops were all moved to indignation, broke his force at Pingjin Pavilion, captured Wenbiao, and dismembered him to eat his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: The army was roused to fury, routed Wenbiao at Pingjin Pavilion, captured him, and dismembered his body for food.

sentences.zh: 初，文表將攻長沙，猶豫未決，有小校夢文表龍出領下，明日以告，文表喜曰：「天命也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wenbiao was about to attack Changsha and hesitated undecided, a junior officer dreamed that a dragon emerged from Wenbiao's collar; the next day he reported it, and Wenbiao rejoiced, saying: "It is Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Before attacking Changsha Wenbiao had hesitated until a junior officer dreamed a dragon emerged from his collar. When told, Wenbiao exclaimed, "Heaven's mandate!"

sentences.zh: 及敗，梟首於朗陵市。

translations.literal: When he was defeated his head was displayed in the market of Langling.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, his head was displayed in Langling's market.

sentences.zh: 荊南高氏高保融

translations.literal: The Gao clan of Jingnan: Gao Baorong.
translations.idiomatic: The Gao of Jingnan — Gao Baorong

sentences.zh: 荊南高保融字德長，其先陝州峽石人。

translations.literal: Gao Baorong of Jingnan, style Decheng, was descended from natives of Xiashi in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baorong of Jingnan, styled Decheng, traced his ancestry to Xiashi in Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖季興，唐末為荊南節度，曆梁、後唐封南平王，卒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jixing was military governor of Jingnan at the end of Tang, passed through Liang and Later Tang enfeoffed as King of Nanping, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jixing had been Jingnan military governor at the end of Tang, served through Liang and Later Tang as King of Nanping, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子從誨嗣，至太傅、中書令，《五代史》有傳。

translations.literal: His son Conghui succeeded him, reaching Grand Tutor and Director of the Secretariat; he has a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His son Conghui succeeded him, rose to Grand Tutor and Director of the Secretariat, and has a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 保融性迂闊淹緩，禦兵治民，一時術略政事，悉委於母弟保勖焉。

translations.literal: Baorong's nature was broad, slow, and dilatory; in commanding troops and governing the people, all contemporary strategy and government affairs he wholly entrusted to his younger brother by the same mother, Baoxu.
translations.idiomatic: Baorong was slow and unworldly; he left all military and civil strategy to his uterine younger brother Baoxu.

sentences.zh: 子繼沖、繼充，繼充至歸州刺史。

translations.literal: His sons were Jichong and Jichong; the latter rose to prefect of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Jichong and Jichong; the second rose to prefect of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弟 保勖

translations.literal: Younger brother: Baoxu.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother — Baoxu

sentences.zh: 保勖幼多病，體貌臞瘠，淫泆無度。

translations.literal: Baoxu from youth had many illnesses; his body was emaciated and thin, and he was dissolute without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxu had been sickly since youth, was gaunt of frame, and dissolute beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 日召娼妓集府署，擇士卒壯健者令恣調謔，保勖與姬妾垂簾共觀，以為娛樂。

translations.literal: Daily he summoned prostitutes to gather in the government offices, chose sturdy soldiers and had them sport freely with the women; Baoxu and his concubines hung curtains and watched together, taking this as entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he gathered prostitutes in the headquarters, paired them with the sturdiest soldiers for ribald sport, and watched with his concubines from behind a curtain for amusement.

sentences.zh: 又好營造台榭，窮極土木之工，軍民咸怨。

translations.literal: He also loved to build terraces and pavilions, exhausting the craft of earth and wood, and soldiers and civilians alike resented it.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved building pavilions and towers to the utmost extravagance, earning the resentment of army and people alike.

sentences.zh: 政事不治，從事孫光憲切諫不聽。

translations.literal: Government affairs went untended; the staff member Sun Guangxian remonstrated sharply but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He neglected government; staff officer Sun Guangxian remonstrated earnestly but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 3 he died at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 廢朝二日，贈侍中，遣禦廚使李光睿賻祭。

translations.literal: Court mourning was observed for two days; he was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, and Imperial Kitchen Commissioner Li Guangrui was dispatched with funeral gifts and sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned for two days; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, and Imperial Kitchen Commissioner Li Guangrui was sent with funeral gifts and offerings.

sentences.zh: 初，保勖在保抱，從誨獨鍾愛，故或盛怒，見之必釋然而笑，荊人目為「萬事休」。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Baoxu was still in swaddling clothes, Conghui alone cherished him; therefore when he was sometimes in great rage, seeing him he would always relax and smile, and the people of Jing called him "All Affairs at Rest."
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while Baoxu was still an infant in arms, Conghui doted on him alone; even in fits of rage, Conghui would soften and smile at the sight of him, and the people of Jing nicknamed the child "All Affairs at Rest."

sentences.zh: 及保勖之立，藩政離弱，卒裁數月遂失國，亦預兆也。

translations.literal: When Baoxu came to the throne, the fief's government was weak and fragmented; within only a few months he lost the state — a portent as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoxu succeeded to rule, the fief's government was already weak and divided; he lost the realm within a few months — an omen, in retrospect.

sentences.zh: 子 繼沖

translations.literal: Son: Jichong
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jichong

sentences.zh: 繼沖字讚平，保融長子也。

translations.literal: Jichong, courtesy name Zanping, was Baorong's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Jichong, whose courtesy name was Zanping, was Baorong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 周顯德六年，以蔭檢校司空，為荊州節度副使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xiande of Zhou, by inherited privilege he was made acting Grandee of Splendid Happiness and deputy military governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Later Zhou's Xiande era, he received the acting rank of Grandee of Splendid Happiness by inherited privilege and was appointed deputy military governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，保勖寢疾，以繼沖為節度副使，權知軍府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, Baoxu fell gravely ill and appointed Jichong military governor deputy with provisional charge of the military government.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong, as Baoxu lay gravely ill, he made Jichong his deputy military governor and gave him provisional charge of the military government.

sentences.zh: 保勖卒，四年正月，製授繼沖為檢校太保、江陵尹、荊南節度。

translations.literal: When Baoxu died, in the first month of the fourth year an edict appointed Jichong acting Grand Guardian, Prefect of Jiangling, and Jingnan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoxu died, in the first month of the fourth year the throne appointed Jichong acting Grand Guardian, Prefect of Jiangling, and military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 時湖南張文表叛，周保權求救於朝廷，詔江陵發水軍三千人赴潭州，繼沖即遣親校李景威將之而往。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Wenbiao rebelled in Hunan; Zhou Baoquan begged the court for aid. An edict ordered Jiangling to dispatch three thousand naval troops to Tanzhou, and Jichong immediately sent his trusted officer Li Jingwei to lead them thither.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Wenbiao rebelled in Hunan, and Zhou Baoquan appealed to the court for help. An edict ordered Jiangling to send three thousand naval troops to Tanzhou, and Jichong at once dispatched his trusted officer Li Jingwei to lead them there.

sentences.zh: 二月，慕容延釗、李處耘等率眾至，繼沖以牛酒犒師，開門納延釗等。

translations.literal: In the second month Murong Yanjiao, Li Chuyun, and others led their forces to arrive; Jichong rewarded the army with cattle and wine, opened the gates, and admitted Yanjiao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Murong Yanjiao, Li Chuyun, and the others arrived with their army; Jichong welcomed the troops with cattle and wine, opened the gates, and admitted Yanjiao and his men.

sentences.zh: 即遣客將王昭濟、蕭仁楷奉表納土。

translations.literal: He immediately sent guest officers Wang Zhaoji and Xiao Renkai to present a memorial surrendering the territory.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent guest officers Wang Zhaoji and Xiao Renkai to submit a memorial offering up the realm.

sentences.zh: 太祖令禦廚使郜嶽持詔安撫，樞密承旨王仁贍為荊南都巡檢使，仍令齎衣服、玉帶、器幣、鞍勒馬以賜繼沖。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered Imperial Kitchen Commissioner Gao Yue to carry an edict of reassurance; Privy Council drafter Wang Renshan was made chief circuit inspector of Jingnan, and he was also commanded to bring robes, jade belts, ritual vessels, and saddled and bridled horses to bestow upon Jichong.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor ordered Imperial Kitchen Commissioner Gao Yue to carry a reassuring edict, appointed Privy Council drafter Wang Renshan chief circuit inspector of Jingnan, and also sent robes, jade belts, ritual vessels, and saddled horses as gifts for Jichong.

sentences.zh: 授繼沖馬步都指揮使，梁延嗣為復州防禦使，節度判官孫光憲為黃州刺史，右都押衙孫仲文為武勝軍節度副使，知進奏鄭景玫為右驍衛將軍，王昭濟左領軍衛將軍，蕭仁楷供奉官。

translations.literal: Jichong was appointed commander-in-chief of infantry and cavalry; Liang Yansi was made defense commissioner of Fu Prefecture; circuit judge Sun Guangxian was made prefect of Huangzhou; right chief military adjutant Sun Zhongwen was made deputy military governor of Wusheng Army; memorial submission director Zheng Jingmei was made general of the Right Brave Guards; Wang Zhaoji was made general of the Left Army Guard; and Xiao Renkai was made a palace attendant officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jichong was made commander-in-chief of infantry and cavalry; Liang Yansi became defense commissioner of Fu; circuit judge Sun Guangxian was appointed prefect of Huangzhou; right chief adjutant Sun Zhongwen became deputy military governor of Wusheng Army; memorial director Zheng Jingmei was made a general of the Right Brave Guards; Wang Zhaoji a general of the Left Army Guard; and Xiao Renkai a palace attendant officer.

sentences.zh: 繼沖籍管內芻糧錢帛之數來上，又獻錢五萬貫、絹五千匹、布五萬匹，復遣支使王崇範詣闕貢金器五百兩、銀器五千兩、錦綺二百段、龍腦香十斤、錦繡帷幕二百事。

translations.literal: Jichong registered and submitted the numbers of fodder, grain, cash, and silk within his jurisdiction, also presented fifty thousand strings of cash, five thousand bolts of silk, and fifty thousand bolts of cloth, and again sent dispatch officer Wang Chongfan to the palace to offer five hundred liang of gold vessels, five thousand liang of silver vessels, two hundred lengths of brocade silk, ten jin of borneol camphor, and two hundred sets of brocade and embroidered curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Jichong submitted a register of the fodder, grain, cash, and textiles under his jurisdiction, also sent fifty thousand strings of cash, five thousand bolts of silk, and fifty thousand bolts of cloth, and dispatched Wang Chongfan to court with five hundred liang of gold vessels, five thousand liang of silver vessels, two hundred lengths of brocade, ten jin of borneol, and two hundred brocade curtain sets.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔鞍轡庫使翟光裔齎官告、旌節賜繼沖，並存問參佐官吏等；

translations.literal: In the third month an edict ordered Saddlery Storehouse Commissioner Zhai Guangyi to bring commissions of appointment and banner-and-tally insignia to bestow upon Jichong, and also to express concern for his staff officers and officials;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the throne ordered Saddlery Storehouse Commissioner Zhai Guangyi to bring Jichong his commission and banner-and-tally insignia, and to inquire after his staff and officials;

sentences.zh: 又以保融兄弟、諸父江陵少尹保紳為衛尉卿，節院使保寅為將作監、充內作坊使，左衙都將保緒為鴻臚少卿，右衙都將保節為司農少卿，合州刺史從翊為右衛將軍，衙將保遜為左監門衛將軍，巴州刺史保衡為歸州刺史，知峽州事保膺為本州刺史，衙將從詵為右衙率府率，從讓為左清道率府率，從謙為左司禦率府率；

translations.literal: Baorong's brothers and paternal uncles were also appointed: Jiangling vice prefect Baoshen as Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; garrison commissioner Baoyin as Director of Palace Construction and director of the inner workshops; left gate chief Baoxu as Vice Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Relations; right gate chief Baojie as Vice Minister of the Court of the National Granaries; Hezhou prefect Congyi as general of the Right Guard; gate officer Baoxun as general of the Left Gate Guard; Bazhou prefect Baoheng as prefect of Gui Prefecture; acting prefect of Xiazhou Baoying as prefect of that prefecture; gate officer Congshen as colonel of the Right Palace Guard; Congrang as colonel of the Left Clear Way Guard; and Congqian as colonel of the Left Imperial Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Baorong's brothers and paternal uncles were also promoted: Jiangling vice prefect Baoshen became Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; garrison commissioner Baoyin became Director of Palace Construction and head of the inner workshops; left gate chief Baoxu became Vice Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Relations; right gate chief Baojie became Vice Minister of the Court of the National Granaries; Hezhou prefect Congyi a general of the Right Guard; gate officer Baoxun a general of the Left Gate Guard; Bazhou prefect Baoheng prefect of Gui; acting Xiazhou prefect Baoying prefect of Xia; gate officer Congshen colonel of the Right Palace Guard; Congrang colonel of the Left Clear Way Guard; and Congqian colonel of the Left Imperial Guard;

sentences.zh: 又以王崇範為節度判官，高若拙觀察判官，梁守彬江陵少尹，韋仲宣掌書記，胡允修節度推官，州縣官悉仍舊，別賜管內符印。

translations.literal: Wang Chongfan was also made circuit judge; Gao Ruozhuo observation judge; Liang Shoubin Jiangling vice prefect; Wei Zhongxuan chief secretary; Hu Yunxiu circuit investigating officer; prefectural and county officials all remained as before; and seals and stamps for the jurisdiction were separately bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongfan was also made circuit judge, Gao Ruozhuo observation judge, Liang Shoubin Jiangling vice prefect, Wei Zhongxuan chief secretary, and Hu Yunxiu circuit investigating officer; prefectural and county officials kept their posts, and new seals for the jurisdiction were granted separately.

sentences.zh: 五月，保紳等來朝，各賜京城第一區。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Baoshen and the others came to court, and each was granted a premier residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Baoshen and the others arrived at court, and each received a premier residence in the capital.

sentences.zh: 六月，命王仁贍兼知軍府事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Wang Renshan was ordered additionally to take charge of military government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Wang Renshan was also given charge of the military government.

sentences.zh: 會是歲將郊祀，表求入覲，可之。

translations.literal: As that year the suburban sacrifice was to be performed, he submitted a memorial requesting an audience at court, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as the suburban sacrifice drew near, he submitted a memorial asking to attend court, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 十月，至闕下，獻金銀器、錦帛、寶裝弓劍、繡旗幟、象牙、玉鞍勒等，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached the capital, presented gold and silver vessels, brocade silks, precious-mounted bows and swords, embroidered banners and flags, ivory, jade saddles and bridles, and the like, and received very generous gifts in return.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reached the capital and presented gold and silver vessels, brocade, jeweled bows and swords, embroidered banners, ivory, and jade saddles and bridles; the gifts he received in return were exceedingly generous.

sentences.zh: 郊禋畢，授繼沖徐州大都督府長史、武寧軍節度使、徐宿觀察使。

translations.literal: When the suburban rites were completed, Jichong was appointed chief secretary of the Xuzhou chief commandery, military governor of Wuning Army, and Xuzhou-Suzhou observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban rites were completed, Jichong was appointed chief secretary of Xuzhou chief commandery, military governor of Wuning, and observation commissioner of Xuzhou and Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 繼沖鎮彭門幾十年，委政僚佐，部內亦治。

translations.literal: Jichong governed Peng Gate for nearly ten years, entrusted governance to his staff, and the region was also well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Jichong governed Peng Gate for nearly ten years, leaving administration to his staff, yet his jurisdiction remained well governed.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年，卒，年三十一。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao he died, aged thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao he died at the age of thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 廢朝二日，贈侍中，遣中使護喪，葬事官給。

translations.literal: Court mourning was observed for two days; he was posthumously granted Palace Attendant; a palace envoy was dispatched to oversee the funeral; and burial expenses were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned for two days; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant; a palace envoy was sent to oversee the funeral; and the state paid the burial costs.

sentences.zh: 自高季興據有荊南、歸峽之地，傳襲三世五帥，凡四十餘年。

translations.literal: From the time Gao Jixing held the lands of Jingnan and Gui and Xia, the line passed through three generations and five commanders, altogether more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Gao Jixing seized Jingnan and the Gui and Xia region, the realm passed through three generations and five rulers over more than forty years.

sentences.zh: 弟 保寅

translations.literal: Younger brother: Baoyin
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Baoyin

sentences.zh: 保寅字齊巽。

translations.literal: Baoyin, courtesy name Qixun.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin, whose courtesy name was Qixun.

sentences.zh: 晉天福七年，以蔭授太子舍人，賜緋，累加檢校司空。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu of Jin, by inherited privilege he was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent, granted scarlet robes, and repeatedly promoted to acting Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Later Jin's Tianfu era he received the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent by inherited privilege, was granted scarlet robes, and rose by stages to acting Grandee of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 兄保融襲封，奏署節院使，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Baorong succeeded to the fief, he memorialized to appoint him garrison commissioner and bestowed upon him gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Baorong succeeded to the fief, he had Baoyin appointed garrison commissioner and granted him gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 宋興，保勖既襲封，遣保寅入覲，太祖召對便殿，授掌書記遣還。

translations.literal: When Song rose, after Baoxu had succeeded to the fief he sent Baoyin to audience at court; the Founding Emperor summoned him for discussion in the informal palace hall, appointed him chief secretary, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty began, after Baoxu succeeded to the fief he sent Baoyin to court; the Founding Emperor received him in the informal palace hall, appointed him chief secretary, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 保寅語保勖曰：「真主出世，天將混一區宇，兄宜首率諸國奉土歸朝，無為他人取富貴資。」

translations.literal: Baoyin said to Baoxu: "A true sovereign has appeared in the world; Heaven is about to unify the realm. Elder brother, you ought to be the first to lead the various states in surrendering territory and returning to the court — do not let others seize the capital of wealth and honor for themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin told Baoxu, "A true sovereign has arisen, and Heaven will soon unite the realm. Brother, you should be first among the regional rulers to surrender your lands and submit to the court — do not let someone else win the credit and rewards."

sentences.zh: 保勖不聽。

translations.literal: Baoxu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxu refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 王師討武陵，道出荊渚，保寅奉牛酒迎犒軍鋒。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Wuling and passed through the Jing region, Baoyin offered cattle and wine to welcome and reward the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched against Wuling and passed through the Jing region, Baoyin greeted the vanguard with cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，驛召赴闕，授將作監，充內作坊使，賜第一區。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor commended this, summoned him by post relay to the capital, appointed him Director of Palace Construction and director of the inner workshops, and granted him a premier residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor praised his conduct, summoned him posthaste to court, made him Director of Palace Construction and head of the inner workshops, and granted him a premier residence.

sentences.zh: 俄知宿州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，丁外艱，起復，轉少府監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande he entered mourning for his father, was recalled from mourning before the period ended, and was transferred to Director of the Palace Handicrafts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande, after his father's death, he was recalled from mourning before the mourning period ended and promoted to Director of the Palace Handicrafts.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，知懷州，曆司農、衛尉二卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he was made prefect of Huaizhou, and passed through the two ministerial posts of Court of the National Granaries and Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao he became prefect of Huaizhou, and later served as minister of both the Court of the National Granaries and the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 是州本隸河陽，時趙普為帥，與保寅素有隙，事多抑製，保寅心不能平，手疏請罷支郡之制，詔從之。

translations.literal: That prefecture had originally been subordinate to Heyang; at the time Zhao Pu was its commander, and he and Baoyin had long been at odds, so many matters were restrained and suppressed. Baoyin could not set his heart at peace, and in a handwritten memorial requested abolition of the system of subordinate prefectures; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: That prefecture had originally been subordinate to Heyang, whose commander was Zhao Pu; he and Baoyin had long been at odds, and Zhao Pu obstructed him at every turn. Unable to endure it, Baoyin submitted a handwritten memorial asking that subordinate prefectures be abolished, and the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 又為西川諸州都巡檢使，改光祿卿，曆知同、汝二州，改光化軍。

translations.literal: He also served as chief circuit inspector of the prefectures of western Sichuan, was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, successively governed the two prefectures of Tong and Ru, and was transferred to Guanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as chief circuit inspector of the western Sichuan prefectures, was made Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, governed Tong and Ru in succession, and was finally transferred to Guanghua Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，賻錢十萬。

translations.literal: Court mourning was observed, and funeral gifts of one hundred thousand cash were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned his death and granted one hundred thousand cash in funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 初，保寅在懷州，蘇易簡、王欽若並妙年始趨學；

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Baoyin was at Huaizhou, Su Yijian and Wang Qinruo were both in their prime years just beginning their studies;
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while Baoyin was at Huaizhou, Su Yijian and Wang Qinruo were both young men just setting out on their studies;

sentences.zh: 在同州，錢若水為從事；

translations.literal: at Tongzhou, Qian Ruoshui served as his aide;
translations.idiomatic: at Tongzhou, Qian Ruoshui served on his staff;

sentences.zh: 在光化軍，張士遜其邑人也。

translations.literal: at Guanghua Army, Zhang Shixun was a native of that place.
translations.idiomatic: and at Guanghua Army, Zhang Shixun was a native of the district.

sentences.zh: 保寅一見皆獎拔，許以遠大，議者多其知人。

translations.literal: Baoyin, upon meeting each of them, encouraged and promoted them all, promising them great futures; commentators widely praised his discernment of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin encouraged and promoted each of them at first meeting, assuring them of bright futures, and many praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 子輔政、輔之、輔堯、輔國，並進士及第。

translations.literal: His sons Fuzheng, Fuzhi, Fuyao, and Fuguo all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Fuzheng, Fuzhi, Fuyao, and Fuguo all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 輔政至秘書丞，輔之至太常丞。

translations.literal: Fuzheng rose to Secretary of the Palace Library; Fuzhi rose to Secretary of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzheng rose to Secretary of the Palace Library, and Fuzhi to Secretary of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 附 孫光憲

translations.literal: Appendix: Sun Guangxian
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Sun Guangxian

sentences.zh: 孫光憲字孟文，陵州貴平人。

translations.literal: Sun Guangxian, courtesy name Mengwen, was a native of Guiping in Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Guangxian, whose courtesy name was Mengwen, was a native of Guiping in Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世業農畝，惟光憲少好學。

translations.literal: The family occupation for generations was farming; only Guangxian from youth loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had farmed the land; only Guangxian loved learning from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 遊荊渚，高從誨見而重之，署為從事。

translations.literal: Traveling in the Jing region, he was seen and esteemed by Gao Conghui, who appointed him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling in the Jing region he impressed Gao Conghui, who took him on as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 曆保融及繼沖三世皆在幕府，累官至檢校秘書監兼御史大夫，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Through three generations under Baorong and Jichong he remained in the staff office, rising by stages to acting Director of the Palace Library and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and was granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the staff offices of Baorong and Jichong through three generations, rose to acting Director of the Palace Library and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and was granted gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 慕容延釗等救朗州之亂，假道荊南，繼沖開門納延釗，光憲乃勸繼沖獻三州之地。

translations.literal: When Murong Yanjiao and others went to quell the rebellion at Langzhou and asked passage through Jingnan, Jichong opened the gates and admitted Yanjiao; Guangxian then urged Jichong to offer up the three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Yanjiao and the others marched to suppress the Langzhou rebellion and sought passage through Jingnan, Jichong opened the gates to Yanjiao; Guangxian then urged him to surrender the three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之甚悅，授光憲黃州刺史，賜賚加等。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, hearing of this, was greatly pleased, appointed Guangxian prefect of Huangzhou, and granted him gifts of an extra grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor was greatly pleased to hear of it, appointed Guangxian prefect of Huangzhou, and rewarded him with especially generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 在郡亦有治聲。

translations.literal: In the prefecture he also had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: In his prefecture, too, he won a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiande he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Qiande.

sentences.zh: 時宰相有薦光憲為學士者，未及召，會卒。

translations.literal: At the time a chief councillor had recommended Guangxian for appointment as Hanlin academician, but before he could be summoned he happened to die.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a chief councillor had recommended him for appointment as a Hanlin academician, but before the summons could be issued, he died.

sentences.zh: 光憲博通經史，尤勤學，聚書數千卷，或自抄寫，孜孜讎校，老而不廢。

translations.literal: Guangxian was broadly versed in the classics and histories and especially diligent in learning; he collected several thousand scrolls of books, sometimes copying them himself, and tirelessly collated texts, never ceasing even in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxian was deeply learned in the classics and histories and devoted to study; he amassed several thousand scrolls, sometimes copying them by hand, and collated texts with tireless care well into old age.

sentences.zh: 好著撰，自號葆光子，所著《荊台集》三十卷，《鞏湖編玩》三卷，《筆傭集》三卷，《橘齋集》二卷，《北夢瑣言》三十卷，《蠶書》二卷。

translations.literal: He loved writing, styled himself Master Baoguang, and authored the Jingtai Collection in thirty scrolls, Gonghu Leisurely Collection in three scrolls, Brush Hireling Collection in three scrolls, Orange Studio Collection in two scrolls, Idle Talk of Northern Dreams in thirty scrolls, and Book of Silkworms in two scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to write and styled himself Master Baoguang; his works included the Jingtai Collection in thirty scrolls, the Gonghu Leisurely Collection in three scrolls, the Brush Hireling Collection in three scrolls, the Orange Studio Collection in two scrolls, Idle Talk of Northern Dreams in thirty scrolls, and the Book of Silkworms in two scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又撰《續通曆》，紀事頗失實，太平興國初，詔毀之。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Continuation of the Comprehensive Calendar, whose record of events was rather untrue to fact; in the beginning of Taiping Xingguo an edict ordered it destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Continuation of the Comprehensive Calendar, which recorded events with considerable inaccuracy; in the early Taiping Xingguo era the throne ordered it destroyed.

sentences.zh: 子謂、讜，並進士及第。

translations.literal: His sons Wei and Dang both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Wei and Dang both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 附 梁延嗣

translations.literal: Appendix: Liang Yansi
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Liang Yansi

sentences.zh: 梁延嗣，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Liang Yansi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yansi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少事高季興，頗見委任。

translations.literal: From youth he served Gao Jixing and was greatly entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he served Gao Jixing and won considerable trust.

sentences.zh: 表授檢校司空、領綿州刺史，充衙內馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: By memorial he was appointed acting Grandee of Splendid Happiness, concurrently prefect of Mianzhou, and commander-in-chief of the inner gate infantry and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial appointment he received the acting rank of Grandee of Splendid Happiness, served concurrently as prefect of Mianzhou, and was made commander-in-chief of the inner gate infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 曆事四帥，人稱其忠藎。

translations.literal: He served four commanders, and people praised his loyal earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: He served four rulers, and people praised his loyal devotion.

sentences.zh: 繼沖之納士也，延嗣亦嘗勸之。

translations.literal: When Jichong surrendered the territory, Yansi had also once urged him to do so.
translations.idiomatic: When Jichong surrendered the realm, Yansi had also urged him to do so.

sentences.zh: 復率荊之水軍從慕容延釗越戰，太祖嘉之，授復州防禦使，充湖南前軍步軍都指揮使兼排陣使。

translations.literal: He again led Jing's naval forces to follow Murong Yanjiao across to battle; the Founding Emperor commended this, appointed him defense commissioner of Fu Prefecture, and made him commander-in-chief of the Hunan vanguard infantry and battle array commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He again led Jingnan's naval forces to join Murong Yanjiao in the campaign; the Founding Emperor praised him, made him defense commissioner of Fu, and appointed him commander of the Hunan vanguard infantry and battle array commissioner.

sentences.zh: 事因郊禮，自復州入朝，太祖慰撫之曰：「使高氏不失富貴，爾之力也。」

translations.literal: When the suburban rites were performed he came to court from Fu Prefecture, and the Founding Emperor comforted him, saying: "That the Gao clan did not lose wealth and honor — that is your doing."
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion of the suburban rites he came to court from Fu, and the Founding Emperor comforted him, saying, "It is thanks to you that the Gao clan kept their wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 改濠州防禦使，有善政，詔書褒美。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defense commissioner of Haozhou, had good policies, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to defense commissioner of Hao, governed well, and received an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 延嗣頗知書，好接士。

translations.literal: Yansi was quite learned in books and loved receiving gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yansi was well read and enjoyed the company of scholars.

sentences.zh: 嘗暴疾，禳於城隍神，是夕，夢神人告以九九之數，俄疾愈。

translations.literal: He once suffered a sudden severe illness and performed exorcism before the City God; that night he dreamed a divine being told him the number ninety-nine, and soon the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: He once fell suddenly and gravely ill and prayed for healing at the City God temple; that night he dreamed that a spirit told him the number ninety-nine, and soon he recovered.

sentences.zh: 開寶九年，卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaibao he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Kaibao at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 漳泉留氏留從效

translations.literal: Zhang and Quan: the Liu clan — Liu Congxiao
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Quan: the Liu clan — Liu Congxiao

sentences.zh: 漳泉留從效，泉州永春人。

translations.literal: Liu Congxiao of Zhang and Quan was a native of Yongchun in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congxiao of Zhang and Quan was a native of Yongchun in Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母兄以孝悌聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he was known for serving his mother and elder brother with filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was known for filial devotion to his mother and respect for his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 頗知書，好兵法。

translations.literal: He was quite learned in books and loved military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was well read and fond of military strategy.

sentences.zh: 唐末，王審知據有福建之地，子延鈞，後唐長興中僭稱帝，國號閩，都福州，為其下所殺，立審知次子延羲。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, Wang Shenzhi held the lands of Fujian; his son Yanjun, in the Changxing era of Later Tang, arrogated the imperial title, with the state name Min and its capital at Fuzhou; he was killed by his subordinates, who installed Shenzhi's second son Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tang, Wang Shenzhi seized Fujian; his son Yanjun arrogated the imperial title in the Changxing era of Later Tang, naming his state Min and making Fuzhou its capital, until his subordinates killed him and installed Shenzhi's second son Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 晉天福末，部將朱文進殺延羲據其位，署其黨黃紹頗為泉州刺史，程贇為漳州刺史，許文稹為汀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianfu of Jin, the subordinate general Zhu Wenjin killed Yanxi and seized his position, appointing his faction member Huang Shaopo prefect of Quanzhou, Cheng Yun prefect of Zhangzhou, and Xu Wenzhen prefect of Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Later Jin's Tianfu era, the subordinate general Zhu Wenjin killed Yanxi and seized power, appointing his ally Huang Shaopo prefect of Quan, Cheng Yun prefect of Zhang, and Xu Wenzhen prefect of Ting.

sentences.zh: 時審知子延政為建州刺史，亦僭稱帝。

translations.literal: At the time Shenzhi's son Yanzheng was prefect of Jianzhou and also arrogated the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shenzhi's son Yanzheng was prefect of Jian and also declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 泉人念王氏失國，群逆分據，時從效為泉州散指揮使，與其黨王忠順、董思安及所親蘇光誨相與圖議，興復王氏。

translations.literal: The people of Quan, remembering the Wang clan's loss of the state and the band of rebels holding separate territories, at that time had Congxiao as miscellaneous commander of Quanzhou; he, together with his associates Wang Zhongshun and Dong Si'an and his close follower Su Guanghui, plotted together to restore the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Quan, grieving the Wang clan's fall and the rebels' partition of the land, found in Congxiao, then a miscellaneous commander at Quan, a leader; with his associates Wang Zhongshun and Dong Si'an and his confidant Su Guanghui, he plotted to restore the Wang house.

sentences.zh: 從效倡言：「吾等皆受王氏恩遇，今王氏子孫未復位而不思報，可謂忠義乎？

translations.literal: Congxiao initiated the declaration: "We have all received kindness from the Wang clan; now the Wang descendants have not yet been restored to their position, yet we do not think to repay them — can this be called loyalty and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao declared, "We have all benefited from the Wang clan's favor; now that Wang's descendants have not yet been restored, can we fail to repay them and still call ourselves loyal?

sentences.zh: 聞建州士卒謀盡力擊福州以復王氏，苟一旦功先成，王氏復位，我輩何麵見之邪？」

translations.literal: I hear the soldiers of Jianzhou plan to exert all their strength to attack Fuzhou and restore the Wang clan; if their achievement should one day be completed first and the Wang clan restored, with what face shall we meet them?"
translations.idiomatic: I hear the troops of Jian plan to throw everything into an attack on Fuzhou to restore the Wang house; if they succeed first and the Wangs return to power, how shall we ever face them?"

sentences.zh: 於是忠順、思安置酒從效家，募敢死士，得陳洪進等五十二人，夜持白梃逾城而入，劫庫兵，擒紹頗斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongshun and Si'an set out wine at Congxiao's home, recruited dare-to-die warriors, obtained fifty-two men including Chen Hongjin, and at night, carrying white clubs, scaled the wall and entered, seized weapons from the armory, captured Shaopo and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhongshun and Si'an held a feast at Congxiao's house, recruited dare-to-die men, and gathered fifty-two followers including Chen Hongjin; that night they scaled the walls with white clubs, seized the armory, captured Shaopo, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 立延政從子繼勳為刺史，從效等三人自署為統帥，洪進等皆為指揮使。

translations.literal: They installed Yanzheng's nephew Jixun as prefect; Congxiao and the other three men appointed themselves commanders-in-chief, and Hongjin and the rest were all made commanders.
translations.idiomatic: They installed Yanzheng's nephew Jixun as prefect; Congxiao and his two companions declared themselves commanders-in-chief, and Hongjin and the others were made military commanders.

sentences.zh: 繼勳令送紹頗首於建州，奉延政為主。

translations.literal: Jixun ordered Shaopo's head sent to Jianzhou and acknowledged Yanzheng as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun sent Shaopo's head to Jian and acknowledged Yanzheng as his leader.

sentences.zh: 延政遂送款於江南李景。

translations.literal: Yanzheng thereupon sent submission to Li Jing of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng then submitted to Li Jing of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 文進率眾攻泉州，為從效所敗。

translations.literal: Wenjin led troops to attack Quanzhou and was defeated by Congxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin marched on Quan with an army but was defeated by Congxiao.

sentences.zh: 會景遣將討王氏之亂，圍福州，兩浙錢氏發兵來援。

translations.literal: At that time Jing dispatched a general to suppress the Wang clan's disorder, besieged Fuzhou, and the Qian clan of the Two Zhes sent troops to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: About then Li Jing sent a general to suppress the Wang uprising and besieged Fuzhou, while the Qian clan of the Two Zhes sent troops to its relief.

sentences.zh: 景將但克汀、建而歸，福州入於錢氏。

translations.literal: Jing's general merely captured Ting and Jian and returned; Fuzhou fell to the Qian clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing's general took only Ting and Jian and withdrew, and Fuzhou fell to the Qian clan.

sentences.zh: 從效以兵劫繼勳送江南，自領漳、泉二州留後，李景即建泉州為清源軍，授從效節度、泉漳等州觀察使。

translations.literal: Congxiao, by force of arms, seized Jixun and sent him to Jiangnan, himself assumed the post of acting governor of the two prefectures of Zhang and Quan, and Li Jing thereupon established Quanzhou as Qingyuan Army and appointed Congxiao military governor and observation commissioner of Quan, Zhang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao seized Jixun by force and sent him to Jiangnan, then took charge of Zhang and Quan as acting governor; Li Jing established Quan as Qingyuan Army and appointed Congxiao military governor and observation commissioner of Quan, Zhang, and the surrounding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 閩中五州自此分矣。

translations.literal: The five prefectures within Min were from this time divided.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the five prefectures of Min were divided among separate rulers.

sentences.zh: 景累授從效同平章事兼侍中、中書令，封鄂國公、晉江王。

translations.literal: Jing repeatedly appointed Congxiao concurrent Grand Councillor, Palace Attendant, and Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffing him as Duke of E and King of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing repeatedly promoted Congxiao to concurrent Grand Councillor, Palace Attendant, and Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffing him as Duke of E and King of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 從效出自寒微，知人疾苦，在郡專以勤儉養民為務，常衣布素，置公服於中門之側，出則衣之。

translations.literal: Congxiao came from humble origins, understood the people's hardships, and in the prefecture devoted himself solely to nourishing the people through diligence and frugality; he usually wore plain cloth, kept official robes beside the middle gate, and put them on when going out.
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao came from humble origins and understood the people's hardships; in office he devoted himself to governing through diligence and frugality, usually wearing plain cloth and keeping his official robes by the middle gate to put on only when he went out.

sentences.zh: 每言我素貧賤，不可忘本。

translations.literal: He often said, "I have always been poor and lowly; one must not forget one's roots."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "I was poor and obscure; one must never forget where one came from."

sentences.zh: 民甚愛之，部內安治。

translations.literal: The people greatly loved him, and within his jurisdiction there was peace and good order.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved him dearly, and his jurisdiction enjoyed peace and good order.

sentences.zh: 王氏有二女嫁為郡人妻，從效奉之甚謹，資給豐厚。

translations.literal: The Wang clan had two daughters married to men of the prefecture; Congxiao served them with great respect and supplied them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Two daughters of the Wang clan had married local men; Congxiao treated them with great respect and provided for them generously.

sentences.zh: 每歲取進士、明經，謂之「秋堂」。

translations.literal: Each year he selected jinshi and mingjing candidates, calling it the "Autumn Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Each year he held examinations for jinshi and mingjing candidates, calling the event the "Autumn Hall."

sentences.zh: 世宗征淮南，李景以兵十萬保紫金山。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, Li Jing held Purple Gold Mountain with one hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, Li Jing defended Purple Gold Mountain with an army of one hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 從效累表於景，言其頓兵老師，形勢非便。

translations.literal: Congxiao repeatedly submitted memorials to Jing, stating that keeping troops stationary long and wearing out the army was not strategically advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao repeatedly memorialized Li Jing, warning that prolonged encampment was exhausting the army and that the strategic situation was unfavorable.

sentences.zh: 既而果敗，江北之地盡入於中朝。

translations.literal: Soon after they were indeed defeated, and all the land north of the Yangtze fell to the Central Court.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon defeated as he had warned, and all territory north of the Yangtze passed into the hands of the central dynasty.

sentences.zh: 從效遣衙將蔡仲贇等為商人，以帛書表置革帶中，自鄂路送款內附。

translations.literal: Congxiao sent yamen generals Cai Zhongyun and others disguised as merchants, placing a silk-written memorial inside a leather belt, and by the Ezhou route submitted allegiance to join the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao sent his yamen generals Cai Zhongyun and others disguised as merchants, with a memorial written on silk hidden inside a leather belt, and by way of Ezhou offered his submission to the central court.

sentences.zh: 又遣別駕黃禹錫間道奉表，以獬豸通犀帶、龍腦香數十斤為貢。

translations.literal: He also sent Vice-Prefect Huang Yuxi by a secret route to present a memorial, offering as tribute a rhinoceros-horn belt with xiezhi design and several tens of jin of borneol camphor.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his vice-prefect Huang Yuxi by a hidden route with a memorial, presenting as tribute a rhinoceros-horn belt patterned with the xiezhi motif and several dozen jin of borneol camphor.

sentences.zh: 世宗錫詔書嘉納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong bestowed an imperial edict commending and accepting it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong issued an edict praising and accepting his overture.

sentences.zh: 從效又乞置邸京師，世宗以其素附江南，慮其非便，不許。

translations.literal: Congxiao again requested to establish a residence in the capital; Shizong, because he had long been attached to Jiangnan, feared it would not be advisable and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao also asked permission to maintain a residence in the capital, but Shizong, mindful that he had long been tied to Jiangnan, judged it inadvisable and refused.

sentences.zh: 宋初，從效遂上表稱藩，貢奉不絕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, Congxiao then submitted a memorial declaring himself a vassal, and tribute offerings never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song, Congxiao formally submitted a memorial acknowledging vassal status, and tribute never ceased.

sentences.zh: 會李景遷洪州，從效疑景討己，頗懼，遣其從子紹錤齎厚幣獻景，又遣使假道吳越入貢。

translations.literal: When Li Jing moved to Hongzhou, Congxiao suspected Jing intended to attack him and was greatly afraid; he sent his nephew Shaoyu bearing lavish gifts to offer to Jing, and also sent envoys asking passage through Wuyue to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing moved his court to Hongzhou, Congxiao feared an attack and grew deeply alarmed. He sent his nephew Shaoyu with rich gifts to placate Jing, and also dispatched envoys to seek passage through Wuyue in order to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 太祖特命使厚賜以撫之，使未至，從效疽發背卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: Taizu specially dispatched an envoy with generous gifts to reassure him, but before the envoy arrived, Congxiao died of a carbuncle on his back at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu specially sent an envoy bearing lavish gifts to reassure him, but before the envoy arrived Congxiao died of a back abscess at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 偽贈太尉、靈州大都督。

translations.literal: The puppet regime posthumously granted him Grand General and Grand Governor of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang regime posthumously ennobled him as Grand General and Grand Governor of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 從效無嗣，以兄從願之子紹錤、紹糸茲為子。

translations.literal: Congxiao had no heirs, so he adopted as sons his elder brother Congyuan's sons Shaoyu and Shaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao had no heirs, so he adopted as sons his elder brother Congyuan's sons Shaoyu and Shaozhen.

sentences.zh: 從效寢疾時，從願守漳州，紹錤在金陵，紹鎡尚幼。

translations.literal: When Congxiao was bedridden with illness, Congyuan was defending Zhangzhou, Shaoyu was in Jinling, and Shaozhen was still young.
translations.idiomatic: While Congxiao lay ill, Congyuan was holding Zhangzhou, Shaoyu was in Jinling, and Shaozhen was still a child.

sentences.zh: 衙校張漢思、陳洪進等率兵劫從效遷東亭，漢思自稱留後，洪進為副使，時建隆三年也。

translations.literal: Yamen officers Zhang Han'en and Chen Hongjin and others led troops to seize Congxiao and move him to Dongting; Han'en declared himself acting military commissioner, with Hongjin as deputy commissioner—in the third year of Jianlong.
translations.idiomatic: Yamen officers Zhang Han'en and Chen Hongjin and others seized Congxiao at swordpoint and moved him to Dongting. Han'en declared himself acting military commissioner and made Hongjin his deputy—this was in the third year of Jianlong.

sentences.zh: 明年，洪進又廢漢思而自立。

translations.literal: The following year, Hongjin again deposed Han'en and established himself in power.
