translations.idiomatic: The next year Hongjin deposed Han'en and seized power for himself.

sentences.zh: 從效再從弟仁譓，淳化中為泗州長史，有清節，官散奉薄，雖藜藿不充，未嘗妄幹人。

translations.literal: Congxiao's second cousin once removed, Renhui, served as Chief Secretary of Sizhou during the Chunhua era; he had upright integrity—his official stipend was meager, and though even wild greens were insufficient, he never presumptuously importuned others.
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao's second cousin once removed, Renhui, served as chief secretary of Sizhou during the Chunhua era. A man of spotless integrity, he lived on a meager salary; even when wild greens scarcely filled his bowl, he never importuned anyone for favor.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，召赴闕，特遷揚州觀察支使。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of this, he summoned him to court and specially promoted him to Branch Commissioner of the Yangzhou Observation Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of this, he summoned Renhui to court and specially promoted him to branch commissioner of the Yangzhou observation commission.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年，從效孫丕式詣闕上從效所受太祖朝制書，授三班借職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Congxiao's grandson Pishi came to court and presented the commission documents that Congxiao had received in the Taizu era; he was granted the acting rank of Third Class Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Congxiao's grandson Pishi came to court and presented the commission documents Congxiao had received under Taizu; he was granted the acting rank of third-class attendant.

sentences.zh: 漳泉陳氏陳洪進

translations.literal: The Chen clan of Zhang-Quan: Chen Hongjin
translations.idiomatic: The Chen Clan of Zhangzhou and Quanzhou — Chen Hongjin

sentences.zh: 陳洪進，泉州仙遊人。

translations.literal: Chen Hongjin was a native of Xianyou in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hongjin was a native of Xianyou in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼有壯節，頗讀書，習兵法。

translations.literal: As a youth he had a bold spirit, read extensively, and studied military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he showed a bold spirit, read widely, and studied the art of war.

sentences.zh: 及長，以材勇聞。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he became known for his talent and courage.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he won renown for his ability and valor.

sentences.zh: 隸兵籍，從攻汀州，先登，補副兵馬使。

translations.literal: He was enrolled in the military rolls; in the attack on Tingzhou he was first to scale the walls and was appointed Deputy Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Enrolled in the army rolls, he took part in the assault on Tingzhou, was first over the wall, and was appointed deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從效卒，少子紹鎡典留務。

translations.literal: When Congxiao died, his youngest son Shaozhen took charge of the acting commissioner's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Congxiao died, his youngest son Shaozhen assumed charge of the acting commissioner's duties.

sentences.zh: 月餘，洪進誣紹鎡將召越人以叛，執送江南。

translations.literal: After slightly more than a month, Hongjin falsely accused Shaozhen of planning to summon Yue men to rebel, seized him, and sent him to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later, Hongjin falsely accused Shaozhen of plotting to summon Wuyue troops in rebellion, seized him, and sent him to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 推副使張漢思為留後，自為副使。

translations.literal: He pushed Deputy Commissioner Zhang Han'en forward as acting commissioner, while he himself served as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He installed Deputy Commissioner Zhang Han'en as acting commissioner and kept the deputy commission for himself.

sentences.zh: 漢思年老醇謹，不能治軍務，事皆決於洪進。

translations.literal: Han'en was old, sincere, and cautious, and could not manage military affairs—all decisions rested with Hongjin.
translations.idiomatic: Han'en was old, honest, and cautious, and incapable of managing military affairs; every decision fell to Hongjin.

sentences.zh: 漢思諸子並為衙將，頗不平洪進，圖欲害之，漢思亦患其專。

translations.literal: Han'en's sons were all yamen generals; they were quite resentful of Hongjin and plotted to kill him; Han'en also worried about Hongjin's monopoly of power.
translations.idiomatic: Han'en's sons, all yamen generals, deeply resented Hongjin and plotted to kill him; Han'en himself also chafed at Hongjin's monopoly of power.

sentences.zh: 明年夏四月，漢思大享將吏，伏甲於內，將害洪進。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following summer, Han'en held a great feast for officers and officials, with hidden armed men inside, intending to kill Hongjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following summer, Han'en held a grand feast for his officers and officials, with armed men concealed inside, intending to kill Hongjin.

sentences.zh: 酒數行，地忽大震，棟宇將傾，坐立者不自持。

translations.literal: After several rounds of wine, the ground suddenly shook violently; the buildings nearly collapsed, and those sitting or standing could not keep their balance.
translations.idiomatic: After several rounds of wine, the earth suddenly shook with great force; the buildings nearly collapsed, and those seated or standing could scarcely keep their footing.

sentences.zh: 同謀者以告洪進，洪進亟去，眾驚悸而散。

translations.literal: A co-conspirator informed Hongjin; Hongjin immediately departed, and the crowd, startled and frightened, dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: A co-conspirator warned Hongjin, who fled at once; the startled assembly broke up in panic.

sentences.zh: 漢思事不成，慮洪進先發，常嚴兵為備。

translations.literal: Han'en's plot having failed, fearing Hongjin would strike first, he constantly kept troops on strict alert as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, Han'en, fearing Hongjin would strike first, kept his troops on constant alert.

sentences.zh: 洪進子文顯、文顥皆為指揮使，勒所部欲擊漢思，洪進不許。

translations.literal: Hongjin's sons Wen Xian and Wen Hao were both regiment commanders; they urged their units to attack Han'en, but Hongjin would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin's sons Wen Xian and Wen Hao, both regiment commanders, pressed their troops to attack Han'en, but Hongjin forbade it.

sentences.zh: 一日，洪進袖置大鎖，從二子常服安步入府中，直兵數百人，皆叱去之。

translations.literal: One day, Hongjin placed a large lock in his sleeve and, followed by his two sons in ordinary dress, walked calmly into the prefectural compound; several hundred personal guards were all ordered away with a shout.
translations.idiomatic: One day Hongjin concealed a heavy lock in his sleeve and, accompanied by his two sons in plain dress, walked calmly into the prefectural compound and shouted away several hundred personal guards.

sentences.zh: 漢思方處內齋，洪進即鎖其門，使人叩門謂漢思曰：「郡中軍吏請洪進知留務，眾情不可違，當以印見授。」

translations.literal: Han'en was then in his inner study; Hongjin immediately locked the door and had someone knock and say to Han'en: "The military officers and officials of the prefecture ask that Hongjin take charge of the acting commissioner's affairs—the popular will cannot be defied; you should hand over the seal."
translations.idiomatic: Han'en was in his inner study. Hongjin locked the door at once and sent a man to knock and call through it: "The officers and officials of the prefecture ask that Hongjin take charge of the acting commissioner's duties. The will of the multitude cannot be resisted—you must hand over the seal."

sentences.zh: 漢思惶懼不知所為，即自門間出印與之。

translations.literal: Han'en, terrified and not knowing what to do, immediately passed the seal out through the gap in the door.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified and at a loss, Han'en immediately passed the seal out through the gap in the door.

sentences.zh: 洪進遽召將校吏士告之曰：「漢思昏耄不能為政，授吾印，請吾蒞郡事。」

translations.literal: Hongjin promptly summoned officers, officials, and clerks and announced: "Han'en is senile and incapacitated for government; he has given me his seal and asked me to take charge of the prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin immediately summoned the officers, officials, and clerks and announced: "Han'en is senile and unfit to govern. He has given me his seal and asked me to take charge of the prefecture."

sentences.zh: 將吏皆賀。

translations.literal: The officers and officials all offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and officials all offered their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 即日遷漢思別墅，以兵衛送。

translations.literal: That same day Han'en was moved to a villa, escorted by armed guards.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Han'en was moved to a country villa under armed escort.

sentences.zh: 遣使請命於李煜，煜以洪進為清源軍節度、泉南等州觀察使。

translations.literal: Hongjin sent envoys to request confirmation from Li Yu, who appointed Hongjin Military Commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and Observation Commissioner of Quannan and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin sent envoys to seek confirmation from Li Yu, who appointed him military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and observation commissioner of Quannan and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時太祖平澤、潞，下揚州，取荊湖，威振四海。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu had pacified Ze and Lu, taken Yangzhou, seized Jing and Hu, and his prestige shook the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: By then Taizu had pacified Ze and Lu, taken Yangzhou, and seized Jing and Hu; his prestige resounded across the realm.

sentences.zh: 洪進大懼，遣衙將魏仁濟間道奉表，自稱清源軍節度副使、權知泉南等州軍府事，且言張漢思老耄不能禦眾；

translations.literal: Hongjin was greatly afraid; he sent yamen general Wei Renji by a secret route to present a memorial, declaring himself Deputy Military Commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and Acting Administrator of the military and civil affairs of Quannan and other prefectures, and stating that Zhang Han'en was old and senile and could not control the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin was deeply alarmed. He sent his yamen general Wei Renji by a secret route with a memorial, declaring himself deputy military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and acting administrator of the military and civil affairs of Quannan and neighboring prefectures, and stating that Zhang Han'en was old and senile and could not command the people.

sentences.zh: 請臣領州事，恭聽朝旨。

translations.literal: He asked that he be allowed to take charge of the prefectural affairs and respectfully await the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be allowed to take charge of the prefecture and to await the court's orders with due respect.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣通事舍人王班齎詔撫諭，又與李煜詔曰：「泉州陳洪進遣使奉表言，為眾所推，因而總領州事，以誠控告，聽命於朝。

translations.literal: Taizu dispatched Palace Interpreter Wang Ban bearing an edict to comfort and instruct him, and also sent an edict to Li Yu saying: "Chen Hongjin of Quanzhou has sent envoys presenting a memorial stating that, having been pushed forward by the multitude, he has thereby taken overall charge of the prefecture; with sincere petition he declares himself subject to the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent the palace interpreter Wang Ban with an edict to comfort and instruct him, and also wrote to Li Yu: "Chen Hongjin of Quanzhou has sent envoys with a memorial stating that, pressed forward by the multitude, he has taken overall charge of the prefecture and, in all sincerity, submits himself to the court's command.

sentences.zh: 觀其傾輸，尤足嘉尚。

translations.literal: Observing his complete devotion, this is especially worthy of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by his wholehearted submission, this is especially worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 但聞泉州昔嘗附麗，尤荷撫綏。

translations.literal: But we have heard that Quanzhou once attached itself to you, and we especially rely on you to soothe and reassure it.
translations.idiomatic: But we understand that Quanzhou was once under your sway, and we especially count on you to soothe and reassure the region.

sentences.zh: 然變詐多端，屢移主帥，恐其地裏遼遠，制禦有所未遑。

translations.literal: Yet with many shifts and deceits, commanders have been replaced repeatedly; we fear that the region, being remote and distant, may be beyond your control in time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with so many shifts and deceptions and commanders replaced again and again, we fear that the region, remote and far away, may be beyond your timely control.

sentences.zh: 朕以書軌大同，恩威遠被，嘉其款附，己降詔書。

translations.literal: We, considering that the written script and cart tracks are unified under one rule and that kindness and majesty reach far, commend their sincere submission and have already issued an edict.
translations.idiomatic: We, believing that writing and cart-tracks are now unified and that kindness and majesty reach far abroad, commend their sincere submission and have already issued an edict.

sentences.zh: 蓋矜其遠俗便安，不必以彼此為意，想惟明哲，當體朕懷。」

translations.literal: This is out of consideration that distant customs may find their own ease—the distinction between 'us' and 'you' need not be made an issue; we trust that your wise understanding will grasp our intent."
translations.idiomatic: This is out of concern that distant peoples should find their own ease; there is no need to make an issue of 'yours' and 'ours.' We trust that your wise understanding will grasp our intent."

sentences.zh: 煜上言：「洪進多詐，首鼠兩端，誠不足聽。」

translations.literal: Li Yu submitted a memorial saying: "Hongjin is full of deceit, wavering like a rat at a crossroads—he truly does not deserve to be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu submitted a memorial saying: "Hongjin is full of deceit and wavers between two sides like a rat at a fork in the road—he truly does not deserve to be trusted."

sentences.zh: 太祖又詔諭之，煜乃聽命。

translations.literal: Taizu again issued an edict instructing him, and Yu then complied.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu issued another edict instructing him, and Li Yu then complied.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, he sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong he sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是冬，又貢白金萬兩，乳香茶藥萬斤。

translations.literal: That winter he again presented ten thousand taels of white gold and ten thousand jin of frankincense, tea, and medicinal herbs.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he again presented ten thousand taels of white gold and ten thousand jin of frankincense, tea, and medicinal herbs.

sentences.zh: 煜復上言，請寢洪進恩命。

translations.literal: Yu again submitted a memorial requesting that Hongjin's favor and appointment be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu again submitted a memorial asking that Hongjin's appointment and honors be revoked.

sentences.zh: 太祖又以諭煜。

translations.literal: Taizu again used this to instruct Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu again sent instructions to Li Yu on the matter.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，製改清源軍為平海軍，授洪進節度、泉漳等州觀察使、檢校太傅，賜號推誠順化功臣，鑄印賜之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, by imperial decree the Qingyuan Army was renamed the Pinghai Army; Hongjin was appointed Military Commissioner, Observation Commissioner of Quan, Zhang, and other prefectures, and Honorary Grand Mentor; he was granted the title Meritorious Minister of Sincere Submission and Harmonious Transformation, and a seal was cast and bestowed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande, by imperial decree the Qingyuan Army was renamed the Pinghai Army. Hongjin was appointed military commissioner and observation commissioner of Quan, Zhang, and neighboring prefectures, with the honorary title of grand mentor, and was granted the title Meritorious Minister of Sincere Submission and Harmonious Transformation; a seal was cast and bestowed upon him.

sentences.zh: 以文顯為節度副使，文顥為漳州刺史。

translations.literal: Wen Xian was made Deputy Military Commissioner, and Wen Hao Prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xian was made deputy military commissioner, and Wen Hao prefect of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，丁家艱，起復。

translations.literal: That summer he entered mourning for a bereavement in the family, then was recalled to duty before the mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he entered mourning for a death in the family, then was recalled to office before the mourning period had run its course.

sentences.zh: 洪進每歲以修貢朝廷，多厚斂於民，第民貲百萬以上者令差入錢，以為試協律、奉禮郎，蠲其丁役。

translations.literal: Every year Hongjin, to maintain tribute to the court, extensively levied heavy taxes on the people: those whose household wealth exceeded one million were required to pay a discretionary sum in exchange for appointment as probationary Harmonizer or Court Gentleman for Ceremonies, exempting them from corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Each year, to maintain tribute to the court, Hongjin levied heavily on the people. Households with assets above one million were required to pay a discretionary sum and were appointed probationary harmonizing director or court gentleman for ceremonies, exempting them from corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 及江南平，吳越王來朝，洪進不自安。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified and the King of Wuyue came to court, Hongjin felt ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan was pacified and the King of Wuyue came to court, Hongjin grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 遣其子文顥入貢乳香萬斤、象牙三千斤、龍腦香五斤。

translations.literal: He sent his son Wen Hao to court with tribute of ten thousand jin of frankincense, three thousand jin of ivory, and five jin of borneol camphor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Wen Hao to court with tribute of ten thousand jin of frankincense, three thousand jin of ivory, and five jin of borneol camphor.

sentences.zh: 太祖因下詔召之，遂入覲。

translations.literal: Taizu thereupon issued an edict summoning him, and he accordingly came to court for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu thereupon issued an edict summoning him, and he set out for an audience at court.

sentences.zh: 至南劍州，聞太祖崩，歸鎮發哀。

translations.literal: When he reached Nanjian Prefecture, he heard that Taizu had died; he returned to his post and proclaimed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Nanjian Prefecture he learned that Taizu had died; he returned to his post and proclaimed mourning.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Hongjin was further given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Hongjin was further granted the honorary title of grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，來朝，朝廷遣翰林使程德玄至宿州迎勞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year he came to court; the court dispatched Hanlin Commissioner Cheng Dexuan to Suzhou to welcome and honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year he came to court; the court sent the Hanlin commissioner Cheng Dexuan to Suzhou to welcome and honor him.

sentences.zh: 既至，賜錢千萬、白金萬兩、絹萬匹，禮遇優渥。

translations.literal: Upon his arrival he was granted ten million cash, ten thousand taels of white gold, and ten thousand bolts of silk—his reception was exceptionally generous.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his arrival he was granted ten million cash, ten thousand taels of white gold, and ten thousand bolts of silk; the honors shown him were exceptionally generous.

sentences.zh: 又增其食邑，以其子文顥為團練使，文顗、文頊並為刺史。

translations.literal: His fief income was also increased; his son Wen Hao was made Regiment Training Commissioner, and Wen Yi and Wen Xu were both made prefects.
translations.idiomatic: His fief income was also increased. His son Wen Hao was made regiment training commissioner, and Wen Yi and Wen Xu were both made prefects.

sentences.zh: 洪進遂上言曰：「臣聞峻極者山也，在汙壤而不辭；

translations.literal: Hongjin then submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that what is highest and loftiest is the mountain—it does not refuse to stand in foul soil;
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin then submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that what is loftiest is the mountain—it does not refuse to stand even in foul soil;

sentences.zh: 無私者日也，雖覆盆而必照。

translations.literal: what is without partiality is the sun—it must shine even upon an inverted basin.
translations.idiomatic: and what is without partiality is the sun—it must shine even upon an overturned basin.

sentences.zh: 顧惟遐僻，尚隔聲明，願歸益地之圖，輒露由衷之請。

translations.literal: Considering how remote and secluded we are, still cut off from your clarifying renown, I wish to return a map of our added territory and hereby lay bare a request from the bottom of my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Considering how remote and secluded we are, still cut off from your clarifying renown, I wish to return a map of our territory and hereby lay bare a request from the bottom of my heart.

sentences.zh: 臣所領兩郡，僻在一隅，自浙右未歸，金陵偏霸，臣以崎嶇千里之地，疲散萬餘之兵，望雲就日以雖勤，畏首畏尾之不暇。

translations.literal: The two prefectures your subject commands lie secluded in a corner; since Zhejiang's right wing had not yet submitted and Jinling held a separate hegemony, with a rugged thousand-li territory and more than ten thousand weary, scattered troops, though I strove to look to the clouds and approach the sun, I had no leisure for anything but fear at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: The two prefectures under my command lie secluded in a corner. While Zhejiang had not yet submitted and Jinling maintained its separate hegemony, with a rugged thousand-li territory and more than ten thousand weary, scattered troops, though I strove to look to the clouds and draw near the sun, I had no leisure for anything but fear at every turn.

sentences.zh: 遂從間道，遠貢赤誠，願傾事大之心，庶齒附庸之末。

translations.literal: Therefore by secret routes I brought afar my loyal devotion, hoping to pour out a heart that serves the greater power and thereby take my place among the least of vassals.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore by hidden routes I brought my loyal devotion from afar, hoping to pour out a heart that serves the greater power and thereby take my place among the least of vassals.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝賜之軍額，授以節旄，俾專達於一方，復延賞於三世。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu granted us a military designation, invested us with the commander's banner and staff, enabling direct communication with one region, and extended rewards through three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu granted us a military designation, invested us with the commander's banner and staff, enabled us to communicate directly with the court from our region, and extended rewards through three generations.

sentences.zh: 祖父荷漏泉之澤，子弟享列土之榮。

translations.literal: Father and grandfather received the grace of a trickling spring; sons and younger brothers enjoyed the glory of fief lands.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers and grandfathers received the grace of a trickling spring; sons and younger brothers enjoyed the glory of fief lands.

sentences.zh: 棨戟在門，龜緺盈室，雖冠列藩之寵，未修肆覲之儀。

translations.literal: Halberds of honor stood at our gate, court robes filled our halls; though we topped the favor shown to feudatories, we never performed the ceremony of appearing at court.
translations.idiomatic: Halberds of honor stood at our gate and court robes filled our halls. Though we stood foremost among the favored feudatories, we never performed the ceremony of appearing at court.

sentences.zh: 暨江表底平，先皇厭世，會嬰犬馬之病，尚阻雲龍之庭。

translations.literal: When the south of the Yangtze was finally pacified, the late emperor passed from the world; I happened to fall ill as a loyal dog or horse might, and was still barred from the dragon-cloud court.
translations.idiomatic: When the lands south of the Yangtze were finally pacified, the late emperor passed from the world. I happened to fall ill like a loyal hound or horse, and was still barred from the dragon-cloud court.

sentences.zh: 皇帝陛下欽嗣丕基，誕敷景命，臣遠辭海嶠，入覲天墀，獲親咫尺之顏，疊被便蕃之澤。

translations.literal: Your Majesty reverently inherited the great foundation and spread abroad the resplendent mandate; your subject came from afar, leaving the sea cliffs, to attend the celestial steps, obtaining close view of your countenance and repeatedly receiving abundant favor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reverently inherited the great foundation and spread abroad the resplendent mandate. Your subject came from afar, leaving the sea cliffs, to attend the celestial steps, obtained close view of your countenance, and repeatedly received abundant favor.

sentences.zh: 六飛遊幸，每奉屬車之塵；

translations.literal: On the imperial progress in the six-horse chariot, I each time followed in the dust of the retinue chariots;
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial progress in the six-horse chariot, I each time followed in the dust of the retinue chariots;

sentences.zh: 三殿宴嬉，屢挹大樽之味。

translations.literal: at banquets in the three halls, I repeatedly tasted from the great wine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: at banquets in the three halls, I repeatedly tasted from the great wine vessel.

sentences.zh: 旬浹之內，雨露駢臻，至於童男，亦荷殊獎。

translations.literal: Within ten days, favor rained down in pairs; even young boys received special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days, imperial favor rained down in pairs; even young boys received special rewards.

sentences.zh: 恩榮若此，報效何階？

translations.literal: Favor and glory such as this—by what steps could I repay them?
translations.idiomatic: Favor and glory such as this—by what steps could I repay them?

sentences.zh: 誌益戀於君軒，心遂忘於坎井。

translations.literal: My will ever more clings to the ruler's canopy; my heart has forgotten the pit of the well.
translations.idiomatic: My will ever more clings to the ruler's canopy, and my heart has forgotten the pit of the well.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝大願，願以所管漳、泉兩郡獻於有司，使區區負海之邦，遂為內地；

translations.literal: Your subject cannot contain his great wish: I wish to offer the two prefectures of Zhang and Quan under my command to the appropriate offices, so that this humble sea-bound region may become inner territory;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject cannot contain his great wish: I wish to offer the two prefectures of Zhang and Quan under my command to the appropriate offices, so that this humble sea-bound region may become inner territory;

sentences.zh: 蚩蚩生齒之類，得見太平。

translations.literal: and the teeming masses of living folk may behold great peace.
translations.idiomatic: and the teeming masses of living folk may behold an age of great peace.

sentences.zh: 伏望聖慈，授臣近地別鎮。

translations.literal: I humbly hope for your sacred compassion in granting me a separate post in a nearby region.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope for your sacred compassion in granting me a separate post in a nearby region.

sentences.zh: 臣男文顯等早膺朝獎，皆忝郡符，牙校賓僚，久經驅策，各希玄造，稍霈鴻私。」

translations.literal: My sons Wen Xian and the others have long received court rewards and all hold prefectural commissions; their military aides and staff retainers have long been driven in your service—each hopes for your mysterious creating grace and a share of your vast private favor."
translations.idiomatic: My sons Wen Xian and the others have long received court rewards and all hold prefectural commissions; their military aides and staff retainers have long served under your command—each hopes for your mysterious creating grace and a share of your vast private favor."

sentences.zh: 太宗優詔嘉納之。

translations.literal: Taizong issued a gracious edict commending and accepting it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong issued a gracious edict commending and accepting the offer.

sentences.zh: 以洪進為武寧軍節度、同平章事，留京師奉朝請。

translations.literal: Hongjin was made Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army and Concurrent Councilor of the same rank, remaining at the capital to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin was made military commissioner of the Wuning Army and concurrent councilor of the same rank, remaining at the capital to attend court.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆授以近郡，賜白金萬兩，各令市宅。

translations.literal: All his sons were given nearby prefectures; they were granted ten thousand taels of white gold each and ordered to purchase residences.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons were given nearby prefectures, granted ten thousand taels of white gold each, and ordered to purchase residences.

sentences.zh: 明年，從平太原。

translations.literal: The following year he accompanied the campaign to pacify Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he accompanied the campaign to pacify Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六年，封杞國公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，進封岐國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi he was advanced to Duke of Qí.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxi he was advanced to Duke of Qí.

sentences.zh: 洪進年老，富貴且極，上言求致仕，優詔免其朝請。

translations.literal: Hongjin was old, his wealth and rank at their apex; he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and a gracious edict exempted him from required court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin was old and his wealth and rank had reached their apex. He submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and a gracious edict exempted him from required court attendance.

sentences.zh: 二年，以疾卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the second year he died of illness at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died of illness at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 廢朝二日，贈中書令，諡曰忠順，中使護喪，葬事官給。

translations.literal: Court business was suspended for two days; he was posthumously made Chief Director of the Department of State Affairs with the posthumous name Zhongshun, a palace envoy escorted the funeral, and burial expenses were provided by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Court business was suspended for two days. He was posthumously made chief director of the Department of State Affairs with the posthumous name Loyal and Obedient; a palace envoy escorted the funeral, and burial expenses were provided by the state.

sentences.zh: 洪進在泉州，日方晝，有蒼鶴翔集內齋前，引吭向洪進。

translations.literal: When Hongjin was in Quanzhou, in broad daylight a gray crane flew and settled before his inner study, stretching its neck toward Hongjin.
translations.idiomatic: While Hongjin was in Quanzhou, in broad daylight a gray crane flew down and settled before his inner study, stretching its neck toward him.

sentences.zh: 洪進視之，有魚鯁其喉，即以手探取之，魚猶活，鶴馴擾齋中數日而後去，人皆異之。

translations.literal: Hongjin looked and saw a fish bone stuck in its throat; he immediately reached in with his hand and removed it—the fish was still alive; the crane stayed tame in the study for several days before leaving, and everyone regarded it as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin looked and saw a fish bone lodged in its throat. He reached in with his hand and removed it—the fish was still alive. The crane remained tame in the study for several days before departing, and everyone regarded it as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 弟 銛

translations.literal: Younger brother: Chen
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother — Chen

sentences.zh: 洪進弟銛，初為泉州都指揮使。

translations.literal: Hongjin's younger brother Chen initially served as Overall Commander of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin's younger brother Chen initially served as overall commander of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，授漳州刺史，入貢至宿州，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao he was appointed Prefect of Zhangzhou; while proceeding to court with tribute he reached Suzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he was appointed prefect of Zhangzhou. While proceeding to court with tribute he reached Suzhou and died.

sentences.zh: 銛子文璉，供奉官、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Chen's son Wen Lian served as Attendant Official and Gate Receptionist.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's son Wen Lian served as attendant official and gate receptionist.

sentences.zh: 子 文顯

translations.literal: Son: Wen Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Son — Wen Xian

sentences.zh: 文顯字仲達。

translations.literal: Wen Xian, courtesy name Zhongda.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xian, whose courtesy name was Zhongda.

sentences.zh: 洪進領漳、泉節制，署左神機指揮使，遷泉州馬步軍都軍使、右軍押衙。

translations.literal: When Hongjin held the Zhang and Quan commands, he appointed him commander of the Left Divine Engines, then promoted him to overall army commander of Quanzhou's infantry and cavalry and right-wing yamen adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: While Hongjin held the Zhang and Quan commands, he made Wen Xian commander of the Left Divine Engines, then promoted him to overall commander of Quanzhou's forces and right-wing yamen adjutant.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，朝命平海軍節度副使，累加檢校太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande the court appointed him deputy military governor of the Pinghai army, and he rose by stages to acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande the court named him deputy military governor of Pinghai, and he rose by stages to acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 洪進歸朝，授文顯通州團練使、知泉州。

translations.literal: When Hongjin came to court, Wen Xian was granted regiment training commissioner of Tongzhou and made acting prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjin submitted to court, Wen Xian was made regiment training commissioner of Tong and acting prefect of Quan.

sentences.zh: 未幾代還。

translations.literal: Before long he was replaced and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and replaced.

sentences.zh: 時太宗征太原，朝於行在。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong was campaigning against Taiyuan, and he presented himself at the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Taiyuan, he presented himself at the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為青齊廬壽、西京水南北、陝州四州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: After a long interval he went out as overall inspector of Qing, Qi, Lu, Shou, the north and south of the Western Capital's waterways, and the four prefectures of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was posted as overall inspector over Qing, Qi, Lu, Shou, the Western Capital waterways, and Shan.

sentences.zh: 文顯與諸弟不睦，咸平初，御史中丞李惟清抗疏曰：「文顯等並分符竹，委以方面，一門榮盛，當世罕儔。

translations.literal: Wen Xian was not on good terms with his younger brothers; at the beginning of Xianping the Censor-in-Chief Li Weiqing submitted a forthright memorial saying: "Wen Xian and the others all hold separate command seals and are entrusted with frontier commands; one family's glory is rare in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xian quarreled with his brothers. Early in Xianping, Censor-in-Chief Li Weiqing memorialized bluntly: "Wen Xian and his brothers each hold a prefectural command — a family's glory rare in our time.

sentences.zh: 先人之墳土未幹，私室之風規大壞；

translations.literal: The grave earth of their forebear is not yet dry, yet the family's private norms are greatly ruined;
translations.idiomatic: Their father's grave is still fresh, yet the household's moral order lies in ruins;

sentences.zh: 弟兄列訟，骨肉為仇，官奉私藏，同居異爨，屢經赦宥，而久積人言。

translations.literal: brothers bring suits against one another and flesh and blood become enemies; official salaries are hoarded privately, they dwell together but cook separately, and though repeatedly pardoned, public talk has long accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: brothers sue one another and kin become enemies; they hoard official salaries, live under one roof but keep separate kitchens, and though repeatedly pardoned, public censure has only grown.

sentences.zh: 文顯首起訟湍，當律文尊長之坐，乞置散秩，以警浮俗。」

translations.literal: Wen Xian was the first to stir up litigation; under the statutes he should bear the penalty for disrespect to an elder — I beg that he be given a nominal rank to warn the frivolous custom of the age."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xian began the lawsuits and under statute deserves the penalty for defying an elder. I ask that he be reduced to a nominal post to warn a frivolous age."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「文顯等頗傷名教，合置邦刑，以其父有忠勳，未忍捐棄，宜賜誡諭，許其改過。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Wen Xian and the others have greatly injured the norms of teaching and names; by rights they should receive the state's punishment, but because their father had loyal merit we cannot bear to cast them off — they should be given admonition and allowed to reform.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Wen Xian and his brothers have gravely offended propriety and deserve state punishment, but their father served loyally and we cannot abandon them — let them be admonished and permitted to reform.

sentences.zh: 倘無悛革，當正簡書，令御史臺告諭之。」

translations.literal: If they do not repent and change, then the written law should be applied; order the Censorate to announce this to them."
translations.idiomatic: If they do not mend their ways, the law will be enforced — let the Censorate deliver this warning."

sentences.zh: 以疾改通許鎮都監。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was transferred to overall supervisor of Tongxu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Illness later moved him to overall supervisor of Tongxu garrison.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子宗憲，曆虞部員外郎，為西京作坊使；

translations.literal: His son Zongxian rose through Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue to workshop commissioner of the Western Capital;
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongxian rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and workshop commissioner of the Western Capital;

sentences.zh: 宗元，殿中丞。

translations.literal: Zongyuan became Palace Secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan became a Palace Secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 子 文顥

translations.literal: Son: Wen Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Son — Wen Hao

sentences.zh: 文顥，初為泉州右軍散兵馬使、衙內都指揮使。

translations.literal: Wen Hao at first was scattered cavalry officer of Quanzhou's right wing and overall yamen commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Hao began as scattered cavalry officer of Quanzhou's right wing and overall yamen commander.

sentences.zh: 俄權知漳州，朝命漳州刺史，凡七年，求還泉州，署行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was acting prefect of Zhangzhou; the court appointed him prefect of Zhangzhou for seven years in all; he requested return to Quanzhou and was appointed campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He soon acted as prefect of Zhang, was confirmed in that post for seven years, then asked to return to Quan and was made campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 開寶末，江南平，洪進遣第三子文顗入貢，文顗不欲行，乃遣文顥。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaibao, when Jiangnan was pacified, Hongjin sent his third son Wen Yi to present tribute; Wen Yi did not wish to go, so Wen Hao was sent instead.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaibao, after Jiangnan fell, Hongjin meant to send his third son Wen Yi as tribute envoy, but Wen Yi refused — so Wen Hao went in his place.

sentences.zh: 至京師，自陳願留以俟父入覲，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital he stated himself willing to remain and await his father's court audience; Taizu commended this.
translations.idiomatic: At court he asked to stay until his father could attend in person; Taizu praised his filial intent.

sentences.zh: 及洪進歸朝，授文顥房州刺史，會升房州為節鎮，換康州刺史。

translations.literal: When Hongjin came to court, Wen Hao was made prefect of Fangzhou; when Fang was raised to a military commission he was transferred to prefect of Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjin submitted to court, Wen Hao was made prefect of Fang; when Fang became a military commission he was transferred to Kang.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，出知同州，錢若水為從事，文顥深禮之，委以郡政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he went out to govern Tongzhou; Qian Ruoshui was on his staff, and Wen Hao treated him with deep respect and entrusted him with the prefecture's administration.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong he governed Tong, where Qian Ruoshui served on his staff; Wen Hao honored him deeply and entrusted him with the prefecture's affairs.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，知耀州，又徙徐州，坐用刑失入，責授左武衛大將軍、知漣水軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he governed Yaozhou, then was moved to Xuzhou; for error in applying punishment he was demoted to Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and made commander of Lianshui army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he governed Yao, then Xuzhou; a judicial error demoted him to Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and commander of Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 上念其父納土效順，復以為康州刺史，留京師。

translations.literal: The emperor, remembering his father's surrender of territory and loyal submission, again made him prefect of Kangzhou and kept him at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his father's surrender of territory, the emperor restored him to Kang and kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，議東封，以濮州馳道所出，命知州事，頓置供擬頗勤至，詔褒之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, when the eastern feng and shan rites were under discussion, because the imperial highway issued from Puzhou he was ordered to administer the prefecture; his hurried preparations of supplies were very thorough, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong Xiangfu, as the eastern feng and shan rites were planned, he was put in charge of Pu Prefecture on the imperial highway; his thorough preparations won imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 駕至，召見勞問。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived he was summoned and comforted with inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession arrived, he was summoned and personally commended.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，改衡州刺史，特給內地刺史奉料，未幾代還。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete he was transferred to prefect of Hengzhou, specially granted the salary allotment of an interior prefect, and before long was replaced and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he was made prefect of Heng with the salary of an interior prefect, then soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 以老疾累表求致仕，詔免朝謁，歲給公費及月廩並如故。

translations.literal: Because of old age and illness he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; an edict excused him from court attendance while annual public expenses and monthly rations continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Age and illness led him to seek retirement repeatedly; the court excused him from attendance while keeping his stipends unchanged.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子 文顗

translations.literal: Son: Wen Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Son — Wen Yi

sentences.zh: 文顗，始為泉州衙內都指揮使、知漳州。

translations.literal: Wen Yi at first was overall yamen commander of Quanzhou and acting prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yi began as overall yamen commander of Quan and acting prefect of Zhang.

sentences.zh: 洪進歸朝，授滁州刺史，仍舊知州。

translations.literal: When Hongjin came to court he was granted prefect of Chuzhou and continued to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjin submitted to court he was made prefect of Chu and kept in office.

sentences.zh: 俄召歸，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and attended court as a regular.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to attend court regularly.

sentences.zh: 景德中，換光州，以久次，領和州團練使，曆知海濮濰沂黃五州、信陽軍，所至無能稱。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era he was transferred to Guangzhou; because of long seniority he held regiment training commissioner of Hezhou and successively governed the five prefectures of Hai, Pu, Wei, Yi, and Huang and Xinyang army — wherever he went he could not win praise.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingde he was moved to Guang; seniority won him regiment training commissioner of He, then turns governing Hai, Pu, Wei, Yi, Huang, and Xinyang — nowhere did he distinguish himself.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 錄其子宗綬為大理評事，孫永弼、永升為三班借職，次子宗纘太子中舍。

translations.literal: His son Zongshou was recorded as reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, grandsons Yongbi and Yongsheng as borrowed third-rank posts, and second son Zongzuan as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongshou was enrolled as reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; grandsons Yongbi and Yongsheng received borrowed third-rank posts; second son Zongzuan became Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子 文頊

translations.literal: Son: Wen Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Son — Wen Xu

sentences.zh: 文頊，本文顯子。

translations.literal: Wen Xu was in origin Wen Xian's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xu was actually Wen Xian's son.

sentences.zh: 初，洪進在泉州，有相者言一門受祿，當至萬石。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hongjin was at Quanzhou, a physiognomist said that one household would receive salaries reaching ten thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: While Hongjin was at Quan, a fortune-teller said the household's combined salaries would reach ten thousand dan.

sentences.zh: 時洪進與三子皆領州郡，而文頊始生，乃以文頊為子，欲應其言。

translations.literal: At that time Hongjin and his three sons all held prefectures and commanderies, while Wen Xu had just been born; Hongjin therefore adopted Wen Xu as his son, wishing to fulfill the prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin and his three sons already held prefectures when Wen Xu was born; Hongjin adopted him as his own son to fulfill the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 初補泉州衙內都校，又為衙內都監使，朝命領順州刺史，歸朝為登州刺史。

translations.literal: He was first appointed overall yamen adjutant of Quanzhou, then overall yamen supervisor; the court ordered him to hold prefect of Shunzhou, and on coming to court he became prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began as overall yamen adjutant of Quan, then yamen supervisor; the court made him prefect of Shun, and after submission he governed Deng.

sentences.zh: 滄、棣有寇盜，命為巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Cang and Di had bandits and robbers he was ordered inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits troubled Cang and Di he was made inspector.

sentences.zh: 會以禁軍大校趙延溥為登州團練使，文頊改舒州刺史。

translations.literal: When the great commander of the palace army Zhao Yanpu was made regiment training commissioner of Dengzhou, Wen Xu was transferred to prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When palace army commander Zhao Yanpu took Deng as regiment training commissioner, Wen Xu was moved to Shu.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，卒，年三十五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he died, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 3 he died at thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 文頊頗知書，亦工畫。

translations.literal: Wen Xu was quite learned in books and also skilled at painting.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xu was literate and skilled in painting.

sentences.zh: 子宗絳，為殿中丞。

translations.literal: His son Zongjiang became Palace Secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongjiang became a Palace Secretariat aide.
